source.title: Revêtements du demi-plan de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands p-adique
readSections: arXiv 1509.00606v2 (28 April 2017, 'Final version, to appear in the Annals of Math'), read in full: 76 pages, SHA-256 bdf8f14fb4bfb4fe43980fdbff088b33469a16a9c0260616a0630de48de8cd68, fetched from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.00606v2 on 23 September 2026 (v1: 2 September 2015). Item locators are v2's pages. The published Annals PDF (91 pages, pp. 321–411, SHA-256 00fb89502da84ea38738734652733ea6487e13686a8e54d32eecf4575d6b0094, from http://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v186-n2-p01-p.pdf; received 19 October 2015, revised 3 March 2017, accepted 5 April 2017, published online 9 August 2017) was used to check every recorded mistake: all five are in the published text, whose pages are also given.

Read: §1 (Définition 1.1, Théorèmes 1.2, 1.4, 1.7, 1.9, 1.10, Remarques 1.3, 1.5, 1.6, 1.8, 1.11), §2 (conventions), §3 (Proposition 3.1 to Remarque 3.7), §4 (Théorème 4.1 to the end of §4.2, Théorème 4.8), §5 (Théorème 5.1 to §5.3), §6 (Définition 6.1 to Définition 6.7), §7 (Théorème 7.1 to Théorème 7.11), §8 (Théorème 8.1 to Théorème 8.8), §9 (Proposition 9.1 to Proposition 9.16), §10 (Théorème 10.1 to Proposition 10.11), §11 (Proposition 11.1 to Remarque 11.13), §12 (§12.1 to Conjecture 12.4), §13 (Lemme 13.1 to the end of the proof of Théorème 5.4) and the references. Recorded mistakes were checked on the page images of both versions.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on Colmez [17], [19], [21], Colmez–Dospinescu [24], Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas [23], Dospinescu [28], [29], [30], [31], Berger [1], [2], Kohlhaase [56], Emerton [33], Schneider–Teitelbaum [70], [72], Frommer [44], Morita [60], Kedlaya [53], Henniart [51], Carayol [11], Boutot–Zink [5], Teitelbaum [81], Grosse-Klönne [46]–[48] and Saito [66] state them as the paper uses them.

summary: Dospinescu and Le Bras prove the Breuil–Strauch conjecture: for π a supercuspidal representation of GL_2(Q_p) with trivial central character and ρ = JL(π), the ρ-isotypic de Rham complex of the Drinfeld tower Σ_n realizes the locally analytic vectors of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence. Theorem 1.2: (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^* ≅ Π^an/Π^lisse for every Π ∈ V(π), unique up to scalar. Theorem 1.4: H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ M_dR(π)^* ⊗ π^*, and the preimage of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π^* in Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ is (Π_ℒ^an)^*, so the Hodge filtration ℒ of the Galois representation is read off the de Rham complex. The proof builds a nonzero Φ globally (Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization and Emerton's local–global compatibility for a definite quaternion algebra), then works locally: Colmez's (φ,Γ)-module theory gives Π(π, 0) = Π^an/Π^lisse, an operator ∂ with a^+ − 1 = u^+∂ (the analogue of multiplication by z), and an O(Ω)-module structure on Π(π, 0)^* via Morita duality (Theorem 1.7); surjectivity of Φ uses Kohlhaase's equivalence between Drinfeld and Lubin–Tate bundles and a functional-analysis lemma on Stein spaces; injectivity and Theorem 1.4 use Π(π, 2) and Colmez's Kirillov model. Corollaries: Theorems 1.9 (Iwasawa cohomology) and 1.10 (infinitely primitivable functions come from Ω), Proposition 12.2. The main line coalesces with the pending Part II of PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp for the geometric realisation in the Drinfeld tower (proposed by Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł, whose étale work quotes this paper); the tower's analytic and de Rham geometry joins the pending ProetaleCohomologyOfPAdicCurvesAndTowers, Schneider–Teitelbaum inputs the pending LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, and trianguline representations the pending TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel; the quaternionic local–global compatibility, Berger's differential equations, Colmez's Iwasawa-theoretic results, Kedlaya's duality and Henniart's types are sources of R31, R06.3, PG.5, RD.1 and R16.2. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 180 items (0 library, 21 planned, 159 missing). 42 mistakes are confirmed (28 misprints, 9 gaps, 5 errors; 4 reach a stated result, 8 a proof). Théorème 1.10 is false as printed: a locally constant function on Σ_0 equal to 1 on one copy of Ω and −1 on the other is a counterexample. It holds with the conclusion f ∈ H^0_dR(Σ_n)·O(Ω), for the components with trivial central character (E9, E40). Théorèmes 1.2, 1.4 and 1.7 stand, with the gaps recorded. Not formalised.

items.name: Admissible Banach representations and their locally analytic, locally algebraic and smooth vectors
items.statement: Ban^adm(G) is the category of representations of G = GL_2(Q_p) on L-Banach spaces Π that have an open, bounded, G-stable lattice whose reduction mod p is smooth admissible in the usual sense (for every open compact subgroup of G, its invariants in the reduction form a finite space). For Π ∈ Ban^adm(G), Π^an (resp. Π^lisse) is the G-stable subspace of vectors whose orbit map G → Π, g ↦ g.v, is locally analytic (resp. locally constant). More generally, for a Banach L-representation B of G, B^an (resp. B^alg, B^lisse) is the subspace of vectors whose orbit map is locally analytic (resp. locally polynomial, locally constant). With Alg(G) the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible algebraic representations of G defined over L and 𝔤 = Lie(G), B^alg is the image of the natural injective map ⊕_{W∈Alg(G)} W ⊗_L Hom_𝔤(W, B^an) → B^an, and B^lisse = (B^an)^{𝔤=0}, the vectors of B^an killed by 𝔤. For K_p ⊂ G an open compact subgroup, B_{K_p−alg} is the image of ⊕_{W∈Alg(G)} W ⊗_L Hom_{K_p}(W, B) → B.
items.note: R30.2 plans the admissible unitary Banach and locally analytic categories for GL_2(Q_p); the density of Π^an is Schneider–Teitelbaum's (item of the locally analytic route).

items.name: Classical local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) (Tate normalization)
items.statement: The classical local Langlands correspondence for G = GL_2(Q_p), normalized as Tate does, attaches to the supercuspidal representation π a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation. Because π is supercuspidal, this parameter is an irreducible 2-dimensional representation of the Weil group with N = 0. Consequently the Weil representation attached to M(π) by Fontaine's recipe is irreducible (used on p. 5). There is a finite extension L of Q_p over which π and ρ = JL(π) are both defined (footnote 6: π is induced from a finite-dimensional representation of an open subgroup that is compact modulo the centre).
items.note: R16.3 imports ET.6's correspondence and compares it with the explicit GL_2 description.

items.name: Local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for D^*
items.statement: To a supercuspidal π of G with trivial central character, the local Jacquet–Langlands correspondence attaches an irreducible finite-dimensional smooth representation ρ = JL(π) of D^*, also with trivial central character and defined over a finite extension L; for π supercuspidal dim ρ > 1.
items.note: R17.1 imports local Jacquet–Langlands and proves the quaternionic rank-two description.

items.name: Fontaine's functor from (φ, N, Gal(K′/K))-modules to Weil–Deligne representations is an equivalence
items.statement: For K′/K finite Galois and L with |Hom_{Q_p}(K′_0, L)| = [K′_0 : Q_p], Fontaine's functor from (φ, N, Gal(K′/K), L)-modules (free K′_0 ⊗ L-modules with bijective semilinear φ, nilpotent N with Nφ = pφN and a commuting semilinear Gal(K′/K)-action) to Weil–Deligne representations of W(Q̄_p/K) unramified on W(Q̄_p/K′) is an equivalence of categories (Breuil–Schneider, Prop. 4.1). Combined with classical local Langlands this attaches to π a (φ, G_{Q_p})-module M(π), free of rank 2 over L ⊗ Q_p^nr.
items.note: R06.3 defines the Weil–Deligne parameter from D_pst and compares conventions; the essential surjectivity is [8, Prop. 4.1].

items.name: Colmez–Fontaine: weakly admissible implies admissible
items.statement: Colmez–Fontaine [22]: weakly admissible filtered (φ, N)-modules are admissible. Hence every weakly admissible filtered (φ, N, G_{Q_p})-module is D_pst of a potentially semistable representation. Applied to M(π) ([8, proof of Th. 5.2]): the Weil representation attached to M(π) is irreducible, so M(π) has no nonzero proper sub-object. Therefore every filtration Fil^{−1} = M_dR(π) ⊃ Fil^0 = ℒ ⊃ Fil^1 = 0, with ℒ an L-line of M_dR(π) (Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1), is weakly admissible. It comes from a potentially crystalline V with D_pst(V) ≅ M(π).
items.note: R06.2 plans weak admissibility versus admissibility.

items.name: Locally algebraic vectors in p-adic local Langlands (Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas)
items.statement: Colmez's functor Π ↦ V(Π) induces a bijection between V(π) and the absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional L-representations V of G_{Q_p} that are potentially crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1 and D_pst(V) ≅ M(π); and det V(Π) = χ_cyc for Π ∈ V(π) since π has trivial central character.
items.note: Cited from [23] (Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas, Camb. J. Math. 2014), which uses Emerton's local–global compatibility; R30.4 plans the comparison of locally algebraic vectors with classical local Langlands.

items.name: Definition 1.1: the set V(π)
items.statement: V(π) is the set of (isomorphism classes of) absolutely irreducible Π ∈ Ban^adm(G) with Π^lisse ≅ π, for π supercuspidal of trivial central character.

items.name: Définition 6.7 (the (φ, Γ)-module N_rig(π))
items.statement: Let K be a finite Galois extension of Q_p containing L such that the inertia subgroup I_K of Gal(Q̄_p/K) acts trivially on M(π), and let K_0 be the maximal unramified extension of Q_p in K. Set N_rig(π) = (R_K ⊗_{K_0} M(π)^{Gal(Q̄_p/K)})^{Gal(K^cyc/Q_p^cyc)}.
items.note: The bijection combines Colmez–Fontaine, weak admissibility and [23, Th. 1.3].

items.name: Drinfeld's moduli of special formal O_D-modules and the half-plane
items.statement: Ω is the Drinfeld half-plane: the rigid space over Q_p with Ω(C_p) = P^1(C_p) − P^1(Q_p). G acts on it through its natural action on P^1(C_p), g.z = (az + b)/(cz + d) for g = (a, b; c, d), where z is 'the' variable on P^1. Write Ω̆ = Ω ⊗̂_{Q_p} Q̆_p. A special formal O_D-module over a Z̆_p-scheme S (with p locally nilpotent) is a formal p-divisible group X over S of dimension 2 and height 4 with an action of O_D, such that the induced action of Z_{p²} makes Lie X a locally free O_S ⊗_{Z_p} Z_{p²}-module of rank 1. Over F̄_p there is a unique O_D-isogeny class of such modules. Fix one, 𝕏. The functor of deformations of 𝕏 by O_D-equivariant quasi-isogenies is representable by a p-adic formal scheme over Z̆_p [Rapoport–Zink]; M̆_0 is its rigid generic fibre. Drinfeld's theorem gives M̆_0 ≅ Ω̆ × ℤ. Under this isomorphism the left action g.(X, ρ) = (X, ρ ∘ g^{-1}) becomes the homographies on Ω̆ together with the shift by −v_p(det g) on ℤ, and the Weil descent datum becomes the canonical one composed with the shift by 1.
items.note: R18.5 plans the Drinfeld upper half-plane, formal moduli and Drinfeld's theorem after Boutot–Carayol.

items.name: The Drinfeld tower Σ_n and its G × D^* action
items.statement: Let X^un be the universal rigid p-divisible group on M̆_0 and n ≥ 1. Then M̆_n = X^un[p^n] − X^un[ϖ_D^{2n−1}] is an étale Galois covering of M̆_0 with group O_D^*/(1 + p^nO_D). The M̆_n form a tower with finite étale transition maps. G acts on every level, and D^* acts by Hecke correspondences that preserve each M̆_n, because 1 + p^nO_D is normal in D^* (footnote 4). For every t > 0 the Weil descent datum becomes effective on p^{tℤ}\M̆_n, where p lies in the centre of G. Σ_n is the resulting model of p^ℤ\M̆_n over Q_p; it carries commuting left G- and right D^*-actions. Σ_n → Σ_0 is finite étale and Galois, with Gal(Σ_n/Σ_0) = O_D^*/(1 + p^nO_D). After base change to Q_{p²}, Σ_0 is two copies of Ω (the paper says simply 'deux copies de Ω'). O_D^* acts trivially on Σ_0 and ϖ_D exchanges the copies. An element g ∈ G acts naturally on Ω and exchanges the copies exactly when v_p(det g) is odd. Finally, O(Ω) ≅ O(Σ_0)^{D^*} through the diagonal embedding.

items.name: Stein spaces: Fréchet structure, de Rham cohomology and duality
items.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 and X a Stein rigid space over K (X has an increasing admissible cover (X_n)_{n≥0} by affinoids with O(X_{n+1}) → O(X_n) of dense image). Then O(X) → lim_n O(X_n) is an isomorphism of topological vector spaces, so O(X) is a K-Fréchet space (in fact a Fréchet–Stein algebra [72]); coherent sheaves on X have no cohomology in degree > 0 (Kiehl [54]). If X is moreover smooth, its de Rham cohomology is the cohomology of the complex of global sections of the de Rham complex, the differentials d^k_X: Ω^k(X) → Ω^{k+1}(X) are strict with closed image, and the H^k_dR(X) are Fréchet spaces [46, cor. 3.2]. If d = dim X, then H^k_c(X, F) = 0 for every vector bundle F on X and every k < d, and H^{k+d}_dR,c(X) is defined as the k-th cohomology group of the complex … → H^d_c(X, Ω^k) → H^d_c(X, Ω^{k+1}) → …. Serre duality for Stein spaces [13] shows this complex is dual to the complex of global sections of the de Rham complex twisted by Ω^d(X), and [47, th. 4.11] if X is pure of dimension d there are canonical isomorphisms H^k_dR(X) ≅ H^{2d−k}_dR,c(X)^* and H^k_dR,c(X) = H^{2d−k}_dR(X)^* (topological duals). Moreover each H^k_dR(X) is isomorphic to the inverse limit of a sequence (V_n) of finite-dimensional K-spaces; hence it is a reflexive Fréchet space, its dual H^{2d−k}_dR,c(X) is the inductive limit of the V_n^*, and H^k_dR(X) is also the algebraic dual of H^{2d−k}_dR,c(X).
items.note: Cited from Grosse-Klönne [46, cor. 3.2], [47, th. 4.11], Chiarellotto [13] and Kiehl [54].

items.name: Proposition 3.1: the Drinfeld tower is Stein
items.statement: For every n ≥ 0, the rigid space Σ_n is a Stein space.
items.note: Ω is Stein and Σ_n → Σ_0 is finite étale.

items.name: The twisted equivariant bundles O(k) on Σ_n
items.statement: For k ∈ ℤ, O^{(k)}(Σ_n) is O(Σ_n) with g.f = (a − cz)^{-k}·(g.f) for g = (a, b; c, d), using the O(Ω)-module structure of O(Σ_n); it is the space of global sections of a G-equivariant bundle O(k), and O(2) ⊗ det = Ω^1 at every level (Ω^1(Σ_n) = O(Σ_n)dz since Σ_n is étale over Σ_0).

items.name: Lemma 3.3 (the G_i-action on O(U_i) is differentiable)
items.statement: For X ∈ 𝔤 and f ∈ O(U_i), X.f = lim_n (e^{p^nX}.f − f)/p^n exists in O(U_i); this makes O(U_i) a 𝔤-module on which f ↦ X.f are continuous endomorphisms of the Banach space O(U_i) (spectral norm).
items.note: Proved on O(U_{0,i}) and lifted along the finite étale U_i → U_{0,i} via minimal polynomials; continuity uses Elkik's theorem [77, lemma 2.5].

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (the G-action on O^{(k)}(Σ_n)^* is locally analytic)
items.statement: For every k ∈ ℤ the action of G on O^{(k)}(Σ_n)^* is locally analytic; equivalently O^{(k)}(Σ_n) is a separately continuous D(G)-module. In particular H^1_dR(Σ_n) is a separately continuous D(G)-module.
items.note: Via the Mahler-type expansions of D(G_2), Frommer's description of D_h(G_i) over U_h(𝔤) and Lemma 3.3. Remark 3.4: the same argument works for coverings of Drinfeld spaces in every dimension [73, Prop. 1].

items.name: Lemma 3.5 (the Lie algebra action on O(Σ_n) in terms of z and d/dz)
items.statement: With ∂ the multiplication by z and u^+ = −d/dz on O(Σ_n), and basis a^+, a^−, u^+, u^− of 𝔤𝔩_2: (a) on O^{(k)}(Σ_n), a^+ = u^+∂ + 1 − k, a^− = −∂u^+, u^− = −∂²u^+ + k∂; (b) on O^{(k)}(Σ_n)^*, a^+ = ∂u^+ + k − 1, a^− = −u^+∂, u^− = −k∂ − u^+∂²; (c) on Ω^1(Σ_n)^*, a^+ = ∂u^+, a^− = −∂u^+, u^− = −∂²u^+; and ∂u^+ − u^+∂ = 1 on all these spaces.
items.note: (a) at level 0 is a direct computation with (gf)(z) = f((dz − b)/(a − cz)) (footnote 25), extended along the étale cover; checked by hand.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (H^1_dR,c(Σ_n) is smooth)
items.statement: The G-representation H^1_dR,c(Σ_n) is smooth.
items.note: Proof of 3.6 (Colmez): by Lemma 3.5(c), any element of Ω^1(Σ_n)^* killed by u^+ is killed by 𝔤𝔩_2.

items.name: Definition 4.3 (p-adic automorphic forms on the definite quaternion algebra B̄)
items.statement: Let B̄ be a quaternion algebra over Q, unramified (split) at p and ramified at ∞, viewed as an algebraic group B̄^* over Q (B̄^*(R) = (R ⊗_Q B̄)^* for every Q-algebra R). Fix an identification B̄^*(Q_p) ≅ G and a compact open subgroup K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ of B̄^*(A_f^p), with K_ℓ ⊂ B̄^*(Q_ℓ) compact open and K_{ℓ_0} torsion-free for at least one prime ℓ_0. Set X = X(K^p) = B̄^*(Q)\B̄^*(A_f)/K^p and, for K_p ⊂ G compact open, X(K_p) = X/K_p = B̄^*(Q)\B̄^*(A_f)/K^pK_p. X is the projective limit of the finite sets X(K_p) and carries a natural right action of G; C^0(X) is the space of p-adic automorphic forms for B̄^*.

items.name: Lemma 4.6 (classical automorphic forms of weight W and p-adic ones)
items.statement: Fix ι: Q̄_p ≅ C (inducing L → C via the fixed L ⊂ Q̄_p). For W ∈ Alg(G), W_∞ = W ⊗_L C is via ι a C-representation of B̄^*(C), hence of B̄^*(R). Let Aut(K^pK_p) be the space of smooth complex-valued functions on B̄^*(Q)\B̄^*(A)/K_pK^p (classical automorphic forms of level K^pK_p), with B̄^*(R) acting by right translation. There is a canonical isomorphism A_{K_p}(W) ⊗_{L,ι} C ≅ Hom_{B̄^*(R)}(W_∞^*, Aut(K^pK_p)), sending f ∈ A_{K_p}(W) to φ_f with φ_f(l)(g) = l(g_∞^{-1}.(g_p.f(g^∞) ⊗ 1)) for g = g_∞·g^∞ ∈ B̄^*(A) and l ∈ W_∞^*.
items.note: As in Taylor [80, §1].

items.name: Global Jacquet–Langlands for quaternion algebras over Q
items.statement: For a quaternion algebra B over Q with ramification set S(B), the global Jacquet–Langlands correspondence is a bijection π ↦ π′ between infinite-dimensional automorphic representations of B^*(𝔸) and automorphic representations of GL_2(𝔸) with π′_v discrete series at every v ∈ S(B).
items.note: R17.3 plans global Jacquet–Langlands.

items.name: Theorem 4.8 (Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization)
items.statement: Let B be a quaternion algebra over Q split at ∞ with discriminant pℓ, B ⊗ Q_p ≅ D, K = K^pK_p with K_p = 1 + p^nO_D, and Sh_K the Shimura curve. For K^p small enough there is an isomorphism of rigid spaces over Q̆_p compatible with Weil descent data B̄^*(Q)\(M̆_n × B̄^*(A_f^p)/K^p) ≅ (Sh_K ⊗_{Q_p} Q̆_p)^an, with B̄ ≅ B away from {p, ∞}, split at p and ramified at ∞.
items.note: Cited from Boutot–Zink [5, Theorem 3.1]; R18.5 plans the uniformization theorem in the Shimura-curve cases.

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (multiplicity of π in the de Rham cohomology of Σ_n)
items.statement: For n with ρ = JL(π) trivial on 1 + p^nO_D: dim_L Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨}, π) = 2; equivalently dim_L Hom_G(π^*, H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ) = 2.
items.note: Global proof after Harris [49] and Fargues [38]: Čerednik–Drinfeld and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Ext^p_G(H^{2−q}_dR,c(Σ_{n,N}), LC(X(K^p))) ⇒ H^{p+q}_dR(Sh_K) (independent of the y_i [38, prop. 4.3.11], D^*-equivariant), whose ρ-part degenerates because H^k_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨} = 0 for k ≠ 1 (D^* acts on geometric components through the reduced norm: Strauch [79] with Faltings–Fargues), giving Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨}, LC(X(K^p))) ≅ H^1_dR(Sh_K)^ρ (2)–(3); then the π(f)^p-isotypic part with Theorem 5.5. Remark 4.2: [68, 78, 62] for Ω; a local proof for the first cover via Teitelbaum's model [81], [61]. Later H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ π^* ⊕ π^*.

items.name: Définition 5.2 a) (Galois representations associated with a Hecke eigensystem)
items.statement: Let φ : T̃_Σ → R be a continuous morphism of topological rings. A continuous representation r : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(R) is associated with φ if det(X − r(Frob_ℓ)) = X² − φ(T_ℓ)X + ℓφ(S_ℓ) in R[X] for all ℓ ∉ Σ.

items.name: Carayol: Galois representations over localized Hecke algebras
items.statement: If r̄ is absolutely irreducible, then for every sufficiently small K_p there is a unique continuous r_m(K_p) : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(T̃_Σ(K_p)_m) associated with T̃_Σ → T̃_Σ(K_p)_m.
items.note: Cited from Carayol [11, th. 3]; R19.6 plans representability over localized Hecke algebras under residual irreducibility.

items.name: Families of p-adic local Langlands (Π^univ)
items.statement: When r̄|G_{Q_p} is absolutely irreducible, the family version of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for G gives an orthonormalizable A-module Π^univ with continuous G-action (an admissible orthonormalizable A[G]-module, as the proof of Théorème 5.4 uses on p. 72) such that Π^univ ⊗_A k(𝔭) ≃ Π(𝔭) for every 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec(A[1/p]); by compatibility with the mod p correspondence, π̄ := Π^univ/𝔪Π^univ is an irreducible smooth representation of G over k_L.
items.note: Cited ([7], [17], [55]); R30.5 plans projective envelopes and their deformation-ring comparison.

items.name: Lemma 13.1 (GL_2(Z_p) acts freely on X with finitely many orbits)
items.statement: The group GL_2(Z_p) acts freely on X = X(K^p) with finitely many orbits. In particular there is s > 0 such that, for every topological Z_p-module M, there is an isomorphism of GL_2(Z_p)-representations C^0(X, M) ≃ C^0(GL_2(Z_p), M)^{⊕s}.
items.note: Density by Mahler's theorem ([63, prop. A.3], [23, prop. 2.12]).

items.name: Proposition 13.5 (the weak local–global statement)
items.statement: For every maximal ideal 𝔭 of A[1/p], Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) ≠ 0.
items.note: After Emerton [33] (p-adic interpolation).

items.name: Theorem 5.4 (Emerton's local–global compatibility for B̄)
items.statement: Under the hypothesis that r̄|G_{Q_p} is absolutely irreducible, for every maximal ideal 𝔭 of A[1/p], C^0(X)[𝔭] ≅ Π(𝔭)^{⊕r} as G-representations for some integer r > 0.
items.note: Due to Emerton [33]; the appendix proves (Π^univ ⊗̂_A M)[1/p] ≅ C^0(X)_m (12) using [33, Lemmas 3.1.16, 3.1.17, B.6, Prop. 3.1.3] and takes 𝔭-parts.

items.name: Breuil's mod p local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) (used for Serre weights)
items.statement: The explicit mod p local Langlands correspondence for G: if r̄_p = Ind_{Q_{p²}}^{Q_p} ω_2^{r+1} (up to an unramified twist) with 0 ≤ r ≤ p − 1, the corresponding smooth π̄ has Sym^r F̄_p² in its GL_2(Z_p)-socle.
items.note: R30.2 plans the mod p classification.

items.name: Henniart: unicity of types for GL_2
items.statement: If a minimal GL_2(Z_p)-type σ of the supercuspidal π embeds in an irreducible smooth representation π′ of G, then π′ ≅ π ⊗ ξ ∘ det with ξ unramified.
items.note: Cited from Henniart [51] (appendix to Breuil–Mézard).

items.name: Théorème 5.5 (a weight-2 quaternionic form with p-component π up to unramified twist, residually irreducible at p)
items.statement: There is a quaternionic modular form f of weight 2 for the group B̄^* such that, if π(f) is the corresponding automorphic representation of B̄^*(A), then π(f)_p = π ⊗ ξ∘det with ξ an unramified character, and r̄_f : G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) is absolutely irreducible in restriction to G_{Q_p}.
items.note: Lemma 5.6 uses a CM form from an imaginary quadratic F with p, ℓ inert and a Hecke character with prescribed reduction at p; the proof prints η̄_p where χ̄_p is meant (sourceIssues E2). The theorem then uses Theorem 5.4 (or Proposition 13.5), exactness of Hom_{GL_2(Z_p)}(−, C^0(X(K^p), O_L/π^n)_m) (Lemma 13.1) and Henniart's unicity of types. After Emerton [33] and [7, Thm 5.1].

items.name: Théorème 5.7 (a reformulation of Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization)
items.statement: There is an isomorphism of Hecke modules Hom_G(LA(X(K^p))^*, Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ) ≅ Ω^1(Sh_K)^ρ, where Hom_G denotes continuous G-equivariant maps.
items.note: Uses Theorem 3.2 (W is locally analytic of compact type) and Lemma 5.9.

items.name: Remark 5.11 (the Hodge filtration under uniformization)
items.statement: The map Hom_G((Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ)^*, LA(X(K^p))) → Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^ρ, LC(X(K^p))) induced by Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ → H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ is identified, via Theorem 5.7 and (2), with the Hodge filtration Ω^1(Sh_K)^ρ → H^1_dR(Sh_K)^ρ.
items.note: Reduced to X_Γ = Γ\M̆_n with the Hodge filtration Im(H^1(Γ, Ω^1(M̆_n)[1]) → H^1(Γ, Ω^•(M̆_n))).

items.name: Théorème 5.1 (a nonzero G-equivariant map Φ)
items.statement: There exist Π ∈ V(π) and a nonzero continuous G-equivariant morphism Φ : (Π^an/Π^lisse)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ.
items.note: From Theorems 5.5, 5.7 and 5.4: Φ_0 : (Π^an)^* → Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ nonzero; its restriction to (Π^an/Π^lisse)^* is nonzero because u^+ kills nothing in Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ, and factors through O(Σ_n)^ρ because H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^ρ is smooth and Π^an/Π^lisse has no nonzero smooth vectors.

items.name: Définition 6.1 ((φ, Γ)-modules over the Robba ring)
items.statement: Let E^{]0,r_n]} be the ring of analytic functions (over L) on the annulus |ζ_{p^n} − 1| ≤ |T| < 1 and R = lim_→ E^{]0,r_n]} ⊂ L[[T, T^{-1}]] the Robba ring, with commuting continuous actions of Γ = Gal(Q_p^cyc/Q_p) and of a Frobenius φ given by φ(T) = (1 + T)^p − 1 and σ_a(T) = (1 + T)^a − 1 for a ∈ Z_p^* (σ_a ∈ Γ with χ_cyc(σ_a) = a). A (φ, Γ)-module Δ over R is a free R-module of finite type with commuting continuous semilinear actions of φ and Γ such that the natural map R ⊗_{φ(R)} φ(Δ) → Δ is an isomorphism.
items.note: PG.2 plans overconvergence and the Robba realization; P7:annulus-foundations the Robba ring.

items.name: Berger's p-adic differential equation N_rig(V)
items.statement: For V de Rham there is a unique sub-(φ, Γ)-module N_rig(V) ⊂ D_rig(V)[1/t] with N_rig(V)[1/t] = D_rig(V)[1/t] and ∇(N_rig(V)) ⊂ t·N_rig(V); with ∂ = t^{-1}∇ it is a p-adic differential equation with Frobenius structure (the construction behind Berger's p-adic monodromy theorem). V ↦ N_rig(V) is not fully faithful: it forgets the Hodge filtration.
items.note: Cited from Berger [1]; R06.3 plans the p-adic-representation to differential-module bridge and the monodromy theorem (RD.2 exports the analytic local monodromy theorem to it).

items.name: Exemple 6.5 (Fontaine–Berger descriptions of D^+_dif, N^+_dif and N_rig)
items.statement: Let V be a de Rham L-representation of G_{Q_p}. For n large the localization map φ^{-n} : D^{]0,r_n]}(V) → (B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{H_{Q_p}} (H_{Q_p} = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^cyc)) is Γ-equivariant and induces an injection D^+_dif,n(V) → (B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{H_{Q_p}}, which gives (Fontaine) a canonical isomorphism of L_n[[t]]-modules with semilinear Γ-action D^+_dif,n(V) = Fil^0(L_n((t)) ⊗_L D_dR(V)) (t-adic filtration on L_n((t)), Hodge filtration on D_dR(V)); via it (Berger) N^+_dif,n(V) = L_n[[t]] ⊗_L D_dR(V) inside D^+_dif,n(V)[1/t]. Moreover N_rig(V) = {z ∈ D_rig(V)[1/t] : φ^{-n}(z) ∈ N^+_dif,n(V) for all n ≫ 0}; for n large N^{]0,r_n]}(V) = {z ∈ D_rig(V)[1/t] : φ^{-k}(z) ∈ N^+_dif,k(V) for all k ≥ n}; and D_rig(V) = {z ∈ N_rig(V)[1/t] : φ^{-n}(z) ∈ Fil^0(L_n((t)) ⊗_L D_dR(V)) for all n ≫ 0}, with a similar description of D^{]0,r_n]}(V) for n large. If V is potentially crystalline, crystalline over a finite Galois extension K of Q_p with maximal unramified subfield K_0, and R_K is the finite étale extension of R attached by the field of norms to K^cyc/Q_p^cyc (Berger's B^†_rig,K; it carries φ and a compatible Gal(K^cyc/Q_p)-action with R_K^{Gal(K^cyc/Q_p^cyc)} = R and R_K^{Gal(K^cyc/K)} = K_0), then (Berger, Marmora) R_K ⊗_R N_rig(V) = R_K ⊗_{K_0} D_cris,K(V) compatibly with all structures, where D_cris,K(V) = (B_cris ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{Gal(Q̄_p/K)} = D_pst(V)^{Gal(Q̄_p/K)}; taking Gal(K^cyc/Q_p^cyc)-invariants, (4) N_rig(V) = (R_K ⊗_{K_0} D_pst(V)^{Gal(Q̄_p/K)})^{Gal(K^cyc/Q_p^cyc)}, so N_rig(V) depends only on the (φ, G_{Q_p})-module D_pst(V), not on its Hodge filtration (and the right side of (4) does not depend on K).
items.note: Cited from Berger [1, 2, th. I.3.3], Fontaine [43] and Marmora [59]; R_K is Berger's B^†_rig,K (field of norms).

items.name: Trianguline representations (Colmez)
items.statement: (Colmez [19]) A 2-dimensional L-representation V of G_{Q_p} is trianguline if, after replacing L by a finite extension, D_rig(V) is an extension of two rank-one (φ, Γ)-modules over R.
items.note: Cited from Colmez [19] (definition; lemme 3.2).

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (∇ has no polynomial kernel on non-trianguline D_rig)
items.statement: For P ∈ L[X] nonzero and V an absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional non-trianguline L-representation of G_{Q_p}, P(∇) is injective on D_rig(V).
items.note: The kernel is finite-dimensional ([30, prop. 2.1]) and φ-stable, so it would contain a φ-eigenvector.

items.name: Kedlaya's duality for p-adic differential equations
items.statement: Let V be a de Rham L-representation of G_{Q_p}, N_rig = N_rig(V), and Ň_rig = N_rig(V̌) the p-adic differential equation of the Cartier dual V̌ = V^* ⊗ χ_cyc. There is a perfect pairing N_rig/∂(N_rig) ⊗ Ň_rig^{∂=0} → L (Kedlaya [53, prop. 20.4.2]; the input is the p-adic monodromy theorem for N_rig).
items.note: Cited from Kedlaya [53, prop. 20.4.2].

items.name: Proposition 6.4 (Colmez: ∂ is bijective on N_rig of a non-trianguline representation)
items.statement: If V is a de Rham, absolutely irreducible, 2-dimensional, non-trianguline L-representation of G_{Q_p}, then ∂ = t^{-1}∇ is bijective on N_rig(V).
items.note: Injectivity by Lemma 6.3 (with t^hN_rig ⊂ D_rig); surjectivity by Kedlaya's duality and the injectivity for the Cartier dual V^* ⊗ χ_cyc. A key observation of Colmez [21].

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (Colmez: D(G)-module structure, duality and the exact sequence for D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1)
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p} and D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 the global sections of Colmez's sheaf U ↦ D_rig(V) ⊠ U (§7.1). (a) The action of G on D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 extends to a structure of topological D(G)-module (D(G) the algebra of distributions on G). (b) If V̌ = V^* ⊗ χ_cyc ≅ V ⊗ δ_V^{−1} is the Cartier dual of V, there is a perfect pairing of topological D(G)-modules { }_{P^1} : (D_rig(V̌) ⊠ P^1) × (D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1) → L. (c) There is a canonical exact sequence of topological D(G)-modules 0 → (Π(V̌)^an)^* → D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 → Π(V)^an → 0, which identifies (Π(V̌)^an)^* with the orthogonal in D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 of (Π(V)^an)^* ⊂ D_rig(V̌) ⊠ P^1 (or of Π(V)^*).
items.note: Cited from Colmez [17, ch. II, IV, V]; R30.3 plans Colmez's construction.

items.name: Theorem 7.3 (Dospinescu: the infinitesimal action of G on D_rig(V))
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p} with generalized Hodge–Tate weights a, b, and k = a + b. By Théorème 7.1 a), U(gl_2) ⊂ D(G) (tensored with L) acts on D_rig(V) ⊠ Z_p = D_rig(V), with Res_U(X·z) = X·Res_U(z) for z ∈ D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1, X ∈ U(gl_2) and U ⊂ Z_p compact open. Take the basis a^+ = (1 0; 0 0), a^− = (0 0; 0 1), u^+ = (0 1; 0 0), u^− = (0 0; 1 0) of gl_2, h = a^+ − a^− = (1 0; 0 −1), and the Casimir C = u^+u^− + u^−u^+ + h²/2 ∈ U(gl_2) (C generates the centre of U(sl_2)); identify f ∈ R with multiplication by f. Then, as operators on D_rig(V): a^+ = ∇, a^− = k − 1 − ∇, u^+ = t, u^− = −(∇ − a)(∇ − b)/t, C = ((a − b)² − 1)/2. In particular, if a = 0 and b = 1: a^+ = ∇ = −a^−, C = 0, u^+ = t, u^− = −∇(∇ − 1)/t = −t∂², where ∂ = t^{−1}∇ is a connection on D_rig(V)[1/t].
items.note: Cited from Dospinescu [28] (Math. Ann. 2012), its main result.

items.name: Definition 7.4 (P-finite vectors and vectors of infinite slope)
items.statement: Let P = (Q_p^* Q_p; 0 1) and let V be a 2-dimensional absolutely irreducible L-representation of G_{Q_p}. a) A vector v ∈ Π(V) is P-finite if there are n, k ≥ 1 with ((1 p^n; 0 1) − 1)^k v = 0 and if L[(Z_p^* 0; 0 1)]v is finite-dimensional over L; Π(V)^{P−fini} denotes the space of P-finite vectors of Π(V). b) A vector v ∈ Π(V)^{P−fini} is of infinite slope if there are n, k ≥ 1 and m ∈ Z with (Σ_{i=0}^{p^n−1} (1 i; 0 1))^k ∘ (p^m 0; 0 1) v = 0; Π(V)^{P−fini}_c ⊂ Π(V)^{P−fini} denotes the space of P-finite vectors of infinite slope.

items.name: Proposition 7.6 (Colmez's Kirillov model)
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional absolutely irreducible L-representation of G_{Q_p}. Then Π(V)^{P−fini}_c and Π(V)^{P−fini} are stable under P, and there is a canonical P-equivariant injection v ↦ φ_v, Π(V)^{P−fini} → LP(Q_p^*, D^−_dif(V))^Γ, where D^−_dif(V) = lim_n D^+_dif,n(V)[1/t]/D^+_dif,n(V), which induces an isomorphism Π(V)^{P−fini}_c ≅ LP_c(Q_p^*, D^−_dif(V))^Γ; in particular v ↦ (φ_v(p^i))_{i∈Z} is a bijection Π(V)^{P−fini}_c → ⊕_{i∈Z} D^−_dif(V).
items.note: Colmez [17, §VI.5]; this form is in Dospinescu [29, Props. 4.6, 4.8, 4.11, Lemme 4.12, Cor. 4.13].

items.name: Proposition 7.7 (the pairing {}_dif)
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p} as in §7.3 and V̌ = V^* ⊗ χ_cyc. The natural pairing V̌ × V → L(1) induces ⟨ ⟩ : D^+_dif(V̌)[1/t] × D^+_dif(V)[1/t] → L_∞((t))dt, where dt is the canonical basis of Q_p(1); put {ž, z}_dif = lim_{n→∞} p^{−n} res_0(Tr_{L_n((t))/L((t))}⟨σ_{−1}(ž), z⟩), where res_0((Σ_{n≫−∞} a_n t^n)dt) = a_{−1}. (a) { }_dif is a perfect Γ-equivariant pairing between D^+_dif(V̌)[1/t] and D^+_dif(V)[1/t]; for n large the orthogonal of D^+_dif,n(V̌) in D^+_dif,n(V)[1/t] is D^+_dif,n(V); hence { }_dif induces a perfect pairing between D^+_dif(V̌) and D^−_dif(V). (b) If V is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1, then for n large the orthogonal of N^+_dif,n(V̌) in D^+_dif,n(V)[1/t] is tN^+_dif,n(V). [The paper states (b) for Hodge–Tate weights 0 and k ≥ 1 with t^kN^+_dif,n(V); with the paper's N^+_dif,n = L_n[[t]] ⊗ D_dR the orthogonal is tN^+_dif,n(V) for every de Rham V, so the printed version fails for k ≥ 2; only k = 1 is used.]
items.note: From [17, before Lemme VI.3.3, Lemme VI.4.16].

items.name: Colmez–Dospinescu: universal completions and the dual of Π(V)^an
items.statement: Π(V)^an determines Π(V); there is m(V) such that (Π(V)^an)^* ⊂ D_rig(V̌) ⊠ P^1 factors through D^{]0,r_{m(V)}]}(V̌) ⊠ P^1 := {z : Res_{Z_p}(z), Res_{Z_p}(wz) ∈ D^{]0,r_{m(V)}]}(V̌)}; Π(V)^an is an increasing union of (1, Z_p; 0, 1)-stable Banach spaces Π^{(h)} by radius of analyticity; Res_{Z_p} induces (Π(V)^*)^{(p,0;0,1)=1} ≅ D(V)^{ψ=1} as Λ(Γ)-modules.
items.note: Cited from [24] (Algebra Number Theory 2014: cor. VI.13, ch. IV, th. IV.6, rem. IV.15, rem. V.14). R30.3 is where the universal completion theorem lives (as PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B's brief imports it).

items.name: Theorem 7.8 (Colmez's duality formula in the Kirillov model)
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional absolutely irreducible L-representation of G_{Q_p}, and let m(V) be such that the inclusion (Π(V)^an)^* ⊂ D_rig(V̌) ⊠ P^1 factors through D^{]0,r_{m(V)}]}(V̌) ⊠ P^1 := {z ∈ D_rig(V̌) ⊠ P^1 : Res_{Z_p}(z), Res_{Z_p}(wz) ∈ D^{]0,r_{m(V)}]}(V̌)} ([24, cor. VI.13]). For n ≥ m(V) and j ∈ Z let i_{j,n} = φ^{−n} ∘ Res_{Z_p} ∘ (p^{n−j} 0; 0 1) : (Π(V)^an)^* → D^+_dif,n(V̌). Then Π(V)^{P−fini}_c ⊂ Π(V)^an, and for all n ≥ m(V), v ∈ Π(V)^{P−fini}_c and l ∈ (Π(V)^an)^*, {l, v}_{P^1} = Σ_{j∈Z} {i_{j,n}(l), φ_v(p^{−j})}_dif, where { }_{P^1} is Colmez's pairing (it induces the natural pairing between (Π(V)^an)^* and Π(V)^an = (D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1)/(Π(V̌)^an)^*), v ↦ φ_v is the map of Proposition 7.6 and { }_dif the pairing of Proposition 7.7.
items.note: Generalizes [17, Prop. VI.5.12]; proved in [29, th. 5.3].

items.name: Proposition 7.9 (P-smooth vectors of infinite slope are smooth)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π) and Π(V)^{P−lisse}_c = {v ∈ Π(V)^{P−fini}_c : u^+v = a^+v = 0} (u^+ and a^+ act because Π(V)^{P−fini}_c ⊂ Π(V)^an, Théorème 7.8). Then Π(V)^{P−lisse}_c ⊂ Π(V)^lisse, and the isomorphism Π(V)^{P−fini}_c ≅ LP_c(Q_p^*, D^−_dif(V))^Γ of Proposition 7.6 induces an isomorphism of P-modules Π(V)^{P−lisse}_c ≅ LP_c(Q_p^*, N^+_dif(V)/D^+_dif(V))^Γ.
items.note: 7.9 from [28, Th. 5.6, Prop. 5.4]; 7.11 uses u^−(1, x; 0, 1) = (1, x; 0, 1)(−x²u^+ + u^− − xh), Π^{(1,Q_p;0,1)} = 0 [29, lemme 7.1] and supercuspidality (identity checked).

items.name: Proposition 8.2 ((Π^an/Π^lisse)^* lies in tN_rig ⊠ P^1)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π), identify V̌ with V, and for n large put tN^{]0,r_n]}(V) ⊠ P^1 = {z ∈ D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 : Res_{Z_p}(z), Res_{Z_p}(wz) ∈ tN^{]0,r_n]}(V)} (and similarly tN_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 = {z ∈ D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 : Res_{Z_p}(z), Res_{Z_p}(wz) ∈ tN_rig(V)}). Then there is n such that the inclusion (Π(V)^an)^* ⊂ D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 induces an inclusion (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^* ⊂ tN^{]0,r_n]}(V) ⊠ P^1.
items.note: From Theorems 7.8, 7.11 and Proposition 7.7.

items.name: The ψ operator on (φ, Γ)-modules over R
items.statement: Every (φ, Γ)-module ∆ over R carries a unique operator ψ commuting with Γ, vanishing on Σ_{i=1}^{p−1}(1 + T)^iφ(∆) and with ψ ∘ φ = id; on D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1, Res_{Z_p} ∘ (p^{−1}, 0; 0, 1) = ψ ∘ Res_{Z_p}.
items.note: PG.4 plans ψ with its continuity and Γ-compatibility.

items.name: Colmez: D(Γ) ⊗_{Λ(Γ)} D(V)^{ψ=1} ≅ D_rig(V)^{ψ=1} ([17, prop. V.1.18])
items.statement: Let V be an L-representation of G_{Q_p} (applied to V ∈ V(π)), D(V) its étale (φ, Γ)-module over Fontaine's ring E [41], Λ(Γ) the algebra of L-valued measures on Γ and D(Γ) the algebra of distributions on Γ. The natural map D(Γ) ⊗_{Λ(Γ)} D(V)^{ψ=1} → D_rig(V)^{ψ=1} is an isomorphism of D(Γ)-modules.
items.note: Cited from Colmez [17].

items.name: Theorem 8.3 ((p, 0; 0, 1)-invariants of (Π^an/Π^lisse)^*)
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π), [(Π(V)^an)^*]^{(p,0;0,1)=1} ⊂ D_rig(V)^{ψ=1} (via Res_{Z_p}) is an isomorphism of D(Γ)-modules, and it induces [(Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^*]^{(p,0;0,1)=1} ≅ (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=1}; composing with Res_{Z_p^*}, [(Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^*]^{(p,0;0,1)=1} ≅ (1 − φ)(tN_rig(V))^{ψ=1}.
items.note: Uses D_rig(V)^{φ=1} = 0 (V non-trianguline).

items.name: Proposition 8.4 a) (w-stability of (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0})
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π). The subspace tN_rig(V) ⊠ Z_p^* := (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0} is stable under the involution w = (0 1; 1 0) of D_rig(V) ⊠ Z_p^* = D_rig(V)^{ψ=0}.
items.note: (a) via Theorem 8.3, trivial central character, generation of (tN_rig)^{ψ=0} by (1 − φ)(tN_rig)^{ψ=1} as a D(Γ)-module ([52, prop. 4.3.8]) and w ∘ σ_a = σ_{a^{-1}} ∘ w; previously proved in [17, ch. VI] and [21].

items.name: Theorem 8.5 (Colmez: the involution on (tN_rig(π))^{ψ=0} is independent of V)
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π) and D_pst(V) ≅ M(π) (inducing N_rig(V) ≅ N_rig(π)), the involution of (tN_rig(π))^{ψ=0} induced by w on (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0} depends neither on V nor on the isomorphism.
items.note: Cited: Colmez [17, §VI.9] (indirectly) and [21] (directly, via the infinitesimal action).

items.name: Colmez's sheaf U ↦ tN_rig(π) ⊠ U and the embeddings of (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^*
items.statement: The involution of Theorem 8.5 and Colmez's recipe [17, §II.2] give a G-equivariant sheaf U ↦ tN_rig(π) ⊠ U on P^1(Q_p) with sections tN_rig(π) on Z_p and P^+ acting by (p^ka, b; 0, 1)z = (1 + T)^bσ_a(φ^k(z)) (a priori equivariant for the free group on P^+ and w; the relations of G hold because they hold for D_rig(V)). A choice D_pst(V) ≅ M(π) gives, up to scalar, G-isomorphisms tN_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 ≅ tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 and G-embeddings tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 ⊂ D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 and (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^* ⊂ tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1.

items.name: Theorem 8.6 (Colmez: (Π^an/Π^lisse)^* does not depend on V ∈ V(π))
items.statement: Let V_1, V_2 ∈ V(π). Then (Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_1)^lisse)^* = (Π(V_2)^an/Π(V_2)^lisse)^* inside tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 (for the G-equivariant inclusions (Π(V_i)^an/Π(V_i)^lisse)^* ⊂ tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1, canonical up to scalar, constructed before the theorem). Hence there is an isomorphism Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_1)^lisse ≅ Π(V_2)^an/Π(V_2)^lisse, canonical up to scalar.
items.note: Due to Colmez [17, th. VI.6.43], [21]; new proof: u^+(Π_1^an)^* and (Π_2^an)^* are orthogonal by rescaling with (p^n, 0; 0, 1) on unit balls (a trick from [21]), then Theorems 7.8, 7.11, Propositions 7.6, 7.7.

items.name: Definition 8.7: Π(π, 0)
items.statement: Π(π, 0)^* is the sub-G-module of tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 which is the image of (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^* for any V ∈ V(π) and any D_pst(V) ≅ M(π); Π(π, 0) is its topological dual with the dual G-action, a locally analytic representation on a space of compact type, with Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse ≅ Π(π, 0) canonically up to scalar.

items.name: Colmez: Π(π, 0) is topologically irreducible
items.statement: The locally analytic representation Π(π, 0) is topologically irreducible.
items.note: Cited from Colmez [21]; it gives the injectivity of Φ directly, but the paper's own proof of injectivity avoids it.

items.name: Proposition 9.1 (u^+ has closed image on (Π^an)^*)
items.statement: Fix Π ∈ V(π), V = V(Π), D_rig = D_rig(V), with (Π^an)^* ⊂ D_rig ⊠ P^1. The operator u^+ has closed image on (Π^an)^* and induces a homeomorphism between (Π^an)^* and u^+((Π^an)^*).
items.note: Uses u^+(x, y) = (tx, −t∂²y) (Theorem 7.3), Proposition 6.4 and open mapping theorems. Remark 9.2 asserts, with a sketched counterexample via [70, ch. 5], that aM need not be closed in a coadmissible module over a noncommutative Fréchet–Stein algebra.

items.name: Théorème 9.4 (the operator ∂ on Π(π, 0)^*)
items.statement: There is a unique continuous linear map ∂ : Π(π, 0)^* → Π(π, 0)^* such that a^+ − 1 = u^+ ∘ ∂ as operators on Π(π, 0)^*.
items.note: Due to Colmez [21]; new proof via Corollary 9.3, the vanishing Casimir and Theorem 7.11 (Casimir identity checked).

items.name: Proposition 9.6 a) (u^+ and ∂ determine the 𝔰𝔩_2-action on Π(π, 0)^*)
items.statement: As operators on Π(π, 0)^*: a^+ = ∂ ∘ u^+, ∂u^+ − u^+∂ = 1, and u^− = −∂a^+ = −∂²u^+.

items.name: Théorème 9.7 (G conjugates ∂ by homographies)
items.statement: For every g = (a, b; c, d) ∈ G, the operator a − c∂ is invertible on Π(π, 0)^*, and g ∘ ∂ ∘ g^{-1} = (d∂ − b)(a − c∂)^{-1} and g u^+ g^{-1} = (det g)^{-1}(a − c∂)² u^+.
items.note: From the identities ga^+g^{-1} = (ad a^+ − ab u^+ + cd u^− − bc a^−)/det g and gu^+g^{-1} = (−ac h + a²u^+ − c²u^−)/det g in D(G) (checked).

items.name: Proposition 9.10 (resolvent matrix coefficients are locally analytic)
items.statement: Let ⟨ , ⟩ be the canonical pairing between Π(π, 0)^* and Π(π, 0). For v ∈ Π(π, 0) and l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*, the map φ_{l,v} : Q_p → L, φ_{l,v}(x) = ⟨(∂ − x)^{-1}l, v⟩, extends to a locally analytic function on P^1(Q_p) that vanishes at infinity.
items.note: Analyticity near 0 uses the filtration Π(π, 0)^{(h)} by radius of analyticity ([24, ch. IV, th. IV.6, rem. IV.15]); Lemma 9.11 checked.

items.name: Proposition 9.12 (Morita duality)
items.statement: Let St^an = LA(P^1(Q_p))/L be the locally analytic Steinberg representation. (a) For λ ∈ O(Ω)^*, the function f_λ defined for x ∈ Q_p by f_λ(x) = λ(1/(z − x)) extends to a locally analytic function on P^1(Q_p) that vanishes at infinity, and λ ↦ f_λ induces an isomorphism of topological L-vector spaces O(Ω)^* ≃ St^an. By footnote 46 this is even an isomorphism of G-representations if O(Ω) is replaced by Ω^1(Ω); p. 9 states it as Ω^1(Ω) ≃ (St^an)^*, µ ↦ (∫ µ(x)/(z − x)) dz. (b) Via O(Ω)^** = O(Ω), the transpose of this isomorphism is µ ↦ f_µ ∈ O(Ω), f_µ(z) = ∫_{P^1(Q_p)} µ(x)/(z − x).
items.note: Cited from Morita [60] (see also [69]).

items.name: Définition 9.13 (the operators T_f for f ∈ S)
items.statement: For f = Σ_{x∈Q_p} a_x/(z − x) ∈ S, T_f : Π(π, 0)^* → Π(π, 0)^* is the continuous linear operator T_f(l) = Σ_{x∈Q_p} a_x(∂ − x)^{-1}(l); it makes sense by Théorème 9.7. By construction, for l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*, v ∈ Π(π, 0) and f ∈ S, ⟨T_f(l), v⟩ = Σ a_x φ_{l,v}(x) = ∫_{P^1(Q_p)} φ_{l,v} µ_f (7), since φ_{l,v} vanishes at infinity.
items.note: Uses Lemma 5.10, Banach–Steinhaus and reflexivity of Π(π, 0).

items.name: Theorem 9.9 = Theorem 1.7 (the O(Ω)-module structure on Π(π, 0)^*)
items.statement: There is a unique structure of O(Ω)-module on Π(π, 0)^* that is compatible with its structure of L-vector space and such that z·l = ∂(l) for all l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*. Théorème 1.7 says the same for every Π ∈ V(π). The structure is given by f·l = T_f(l) (Propositions 9.14–9.15); in the notation of p. 9, (∫_{P^1(Q_p)} µ(x)/(z − x))·l = ∫_{P^1(Q_p)} (∂ − x)^{-1}(l) µ(x).

items.name: Proposition 9.16 (G-equivariant maps are O(Ω)-linear)
items.statement: Every continuous G-equivariant Φ : Π(π, 0)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ is O(Ω)-linear.
items.note: Both sides satisfy a^+ − 1 = u^+∂ and u^+ is injective on O(Σ_n)^ρ.

items.name: Lemma 10.2 (dense image descends from Q̆_p)
items.statement: If F : X → Y is a continuous map of Fréchet spaces over Q_p such that F̆ : X̆ → Y̆ (completed base change to Q̆_p) has dense image, then F has dense image.

items.name: Kohlhaase's Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld bundles
items.statement: Let M̆_0^{(0)} be the height-0 component of M̆_0 with coverings M̆_n^{(0)}, and L̆_0^{(0)} the Lubin–Tate space (an open unit ball) with Galois coverings L̆_n^{(0)} of group G_0/G_n; O(M̆_n^{(0)}) is (F̆_n, G_n)-regular and O(L̆_n^{(0)}) is (F̆_n, D_n)-regular. For a G_0-equivariant bundle N on M̆_0^{(0)} with sections N, Λ_n(N) = (O(M̆_n^{(0)}) ⊗ N)^{G_n} and O(M̆_n^{(0)}) ⊗_{F̆_n} Λ_n(N) → O(M̆_n^{(0)}) ⊗ N (8) is injective; N is Lubin–Tate if (8) is an isomorphism for some n, and then D_LT(N) is the D_0-equivariant bundle on L̆_0^{(0)} with sections (O(L̆_n^{(0)}) ⊗_{F̆_n} Λ_n(N))^{G_0}; symmetrically ∆_n, (9), Drinfeld bundles and D_Dr (Definition 10.4). A G-equivariant bundle on Ω̆ (resp. D^*-equivariant bundle on P̆^1) is Lubin–Tate (resp. Drinfeld) if its pullback along the period map π_Dr^{(0)} (resp. the Gross–Hopkins period map π_LT^{(0)}) is; then D_LT(N) (resp. D_Dr(N)) is D^*- (resp. G-) equivariant and descends to P̆^1 (resp. Ω̆).
items.note: After Kohlhaase [56]; the Lubin–Tate tower's construction is ET.6a's, the Gross–Hopkins period map is [45].

items.name: Theorem 10.5 (Kohlhaase: Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld bundles are equivalent)
items.statement: (a) D_LT and D_Dr are equivalences of categories, quasi-inverse to each other, between the G-equivariant Lubin–Tate bundles on Ω̆ and the D^*-equivariant Drinfeld bundles on P̆^1. (b) If ρ is a smooth finite-dimensional representation of D^*, then ρ^* ⊗ O_{P̆^1} is a Drinfeld bundle and there is a canonical isomorphism D_Dr(ρ^* ⊗ O_{P̆^1}) = O(M̆_n)^ρ. (c) The categories of Drinfeld bundles and of Lubin–Tate bundles are stable under subobjects and quotients, and D_LT and D_Dr preserve exact sequences.
items.note: Cited from Kohlhaase [56] (elementary, without the Faltings–Fargues isomorphism; projectivity [56, prop. A5]). Remark 10.7: the smoothness of ρ is essential, cf. 0 → O(−1) → V(X) ⊗ O → O(1) → 0 on P^1 for the Dieudonné module V(X) [45].

items.name: Proposition 10.3 (Φ̆ has dense image)
items.statement: Let Φ : Π(π, 0)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ be a nonzero continuous G-equivariant map (as in Théorème 10.1); it is O(Ω)-linear by Proposition 9.16. Then the image of Φ̆ = Φ ⊗̂ Q̆_p is dense in O(M̆_n)^ρ. The proof shows more: every nonzero closed G-stable O(Ω̆)-submodule of O(M̆_n)^ρ is the whole space.
items.note: Via coadmissible O(Ω̆)-modules, torsion-freeness of G-equivariant coherent sheaves on Ω̆, Theorem 10.5, a twist by O(λ) and the irreducibility of ρ^* ⊗ Sym^λ(L²). Remark 10.9: O(Σ_n)^ρ is irreducible as a G-module (from [21] and Theorem 1.2), not proved here.

items.name: Proposition 10.11 (dense image implies surjective over a Stein space)
items.statement: Let X be Stein over Q_p, N a finitely generated projective O(X)-module and Y an O(X)-module which is a Fréchet space. Every continuous O(X)-linear F : Y → N with dense image is surjective.
items.note: Reduce to a dense ideal I; build f_1, …, f_m ∈ I with no common zero by lowering dim V(f_1, …, f_i) using convergent series in Y and the affinoid Nullstellensatz; finitely generated ideals are closed [72].

items.name: Théorème 10.1 (every nonzero Φ is surjective)
items.statement: Every nonzero continuous G-equivariant morphism Φ : Π(π, 0)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ is surjective.
items.note: From Propositions 9.16, 10.3 and 10.11 (X = Ω, Y = Π(π, 0)^*, N = O(Σ_n)^ρ).

items.name: The representation Π(π, 2)^* (formula (10))
items.statement: Ω^1(Σ_n) is obtained from O(Σ_n) by twisting with the cocycle c ∈ Z^1(G, O(Ω)^*), c(g) = det g·(a − cz)^{-2} for g = (a, b; c, d). By analogy, and using the first part of Théorème 9.7, set g ∗ l = det g·(a − c∂)^{-2}(g.l) on Π(π, 0)^*, and Π(π, 2)^* = Π(π, 0)^* dz with g(l dz) = (det g·(a − c∂)^{-2}(g.l)) dz (10).

items.name: Proposition 11.2 (the Kirillov embedding of (Π^an/Π^lisse)^{u^+=0})
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π), v ↦ φ_v induces a P-equivariant embedding Ψ_V : (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^{u^+=0} → LP(Q_p^*, t^{-1}N^+_dif(V)/N^+_dif(V))^Γ.

items.name: Theorem 11.3 (the Kirillov embedding ι_{V,α} does not depend on (V, α))
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π) and α : D_pst(V) ≃ M(π), let ι_{V,α} = α_dif ∘ Ψ_V ∘ (ξ_{V,α}|_{Π(π,0)^{u^+=0}}) : Π(π,0)^{u^+=0} → LP(Q_p^*, L_∞(−1) ⊗_L M_dR(π))^Γ. Then ι_{V,α} does not depend, up to homothety, on the choice of V ∈ V(π) or of α. Moreover, for every V and α, the square of P-representations whose top row is (a fixed) Π(π,0)^{u^+=0} → LP(Q_p^*, L_∞(−1) ⊗_L M_dR(π))^Γ, bottom row Ψ_V : (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^{u^+=0} → LP(Q_p^*, t^{-1}N^+_dif(V)/N^+_dif(V))^Γ and vertical maps ξ_{V,α} and α_dif^{-1}, commutes up to scalar. In particular there is a P-equivariant embedding, canonical up to scalar, ι : Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} → LC(Q_p^*, L_∞ ⊗_L M_dR(π))^Γ.
items.note: The pairings {}_dif,V_j come from ∧²D_pst(V_j) ≅ L, so change of V rescales them. The proof of 11.4 prints i_{V,α} for ι_{V,α} (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Proposition 11.6 ((Π^an)^* inside Π(π, 2)^*)
items.statement: For Π ∈ V(π), an isomorphism Π(π, 0) ≅ Π^an/Π^lisse determines a G-equivariant embedding of (Π^an)^* into Π(π, 2)^* (l ↦ −u^+(l)dz), making (Π^an)^* a G-stable subspace containing d(Π(π, 0)^*).
items.note: Borel-equivariance from u^+(a, b; 0, d) = (d/a)(a, b; 0, d)u^+ and w-equivariance from w∂^{−2}w = ∂² and u^− = −∂²u^+ (checked); the proof calls the map F for d (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Theorem 11.7 (the kernel of u^+ on Π(π, 2))
items.statement: The subspace Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} of Π(π,2) is stable under G, and there is an isomorphism of G-representations, canonical up to scalar, Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} ≃ π ⊗ M_dR(π) (in particular Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} is smooth).
items.note: Two non-isomorphic V_1, V_2 ∈ V(π) give distinct subspaces X_j ≅ π^* by Colmez–Dospinescu [24], hence Π(π, 2)^{u^+=0} ↠ π^{⊕2}, split since π is supercuspidal; the complement vanishes by the Kirillov model (Theorem 11.3). The proof writes Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_2)^lisse for Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_1)^lisse (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Corollary 11.9 (the position of (Π_ℒ^an)^* in Π(π, 2)^*)
items.statement: Let ℒ be a filtration (an L-line) of M_dR(π), V_ℒ ∈ V(π) the corresponding representation with its isomorphism D_pst(V_ℒ) ≃ M(π), and Π_ℒ = Π(V_ℒ). Then the preimage in Π(π,2)^* of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π^* ⊂ (Π(π,2)^{u^+=0})^* (via Théorème 11.7) is (Π_ℒ^an)^*, viewed inside Π(π,2)^* by Proposition 11.6.

items.name: Proposition 11.10 (injectivity of Φ)
items.statement: Viewed as Φ : Π(π, 2)^* → Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ (Proposition 9.16), Φ is injective.
items.note: The composite to H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ factors through ((Π(π, 2))^{u^+=0})^* ≅ (π^*)^{⊕2}, which must map isomorphically since H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ has (π^*)^{⊕2} as a quotient (Theorem 4.1; footnote 52: π supercuspidal is projective among smooth representations with trivial central character); a kernel element is then infinitely t-divisible in tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1, hence 0. Remark 11.11: ∩_j Im((u^+)^j) = 0 needs [31].

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (the dual of the ρ-isotypic functions on the Drinfeld tower)
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G = GL_2(Q_p) with trivial central character and ρ = JL(π). For every Π ∈ V(π) and every n large enough (ρ trivial on 1 + p^nO_D suffices) there is an isomorphism of topological G-modules, unique up to scalar, (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^* ≅ Π^an/Π^lisse.
items.note: Theorems 8.8, 10.1, Proposition 11.10; uniqueness from Propositions 9.16 and 10.10. Consequence (Remark 1.3(b)): (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^* is an admissible locally analytic representation.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (the de Rham complex of Σ_n: the Breuil–Strauch conjecture)
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G = GL_2(Q_p) with trivial central character, ρ = JL(π), n such that ρ is trivial on 1 + p^nO_D, and M_dR = M_dR(π). There is an isomorphism of Fréchet G-modules, canonical up to scalar, H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ M_dR^* ⊗_L π^*, with the following property. For every L-line ℒ ⊂ M_dR, let ℒ^⊥ ⊂ M_dR^* be its orthogonal and Π_ℒ ∈ V(π) the representation whose Galois representation has Hodge filtration ℒ. Then the preimage of ℒ^⊥ ⊗_L π^* ⊂ H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ in Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ is isomorphic to (Π_ℒ^an)^*. Moreover the resulting exact sequence 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → (Π_ℒ^an)^* → ℒ^⊥ ⊗_L π^* ≅ π^* → 0 is dual to the sequence 0 → π → Π_ℒ^an → Π_ℒ^an/Π_ℒ^lisse ≅ (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^* → 0 given by Théorème 1.2. Here 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ → H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ → 0 is the ρ-isotypic part (σ^ρ = Hom_{D^*}(ρ, σ)) of the de Rham complex of the Stein space Σ_n. It is exact on the left because H^0_dR(Σ_n)^ρ = 0 for dim ρ > 1 ([79], [37]).
items.note: Conjectured by Breuil and Strauch [9] (unpublished; for the first cover). Φ gives (Π(π, 2)^{u^+=0})^* ≅ H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ; combine with Theorem 11.7 and Corollary 11.9.

items.name: Remark 11.12 (twisted coefficients: Hodge–Tate weights 0, k + 1)
items.statement: All results extend to the bundles O(k): Theorem 1.2 with Π(π, 0) replaced by the representation whose dual is Π(π, 0)^* with G-action twisted by (a − c∂)^{−k}, and Theorem 1.4 using, for k ≥ 0, the exact sequence 0 → O(−k)(Σ_n)^ρ →^{(u^+)^{k+1}} O(k + 2)(Σ_n)^ρ ⊗ det^{k+1} → H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ⊗ Sym^k → 0, describing locally analytic vectors for Galois weights 0, k + 1.
items.note: Asserted without details; the exact sequence 'se justifie comme dans [68, pp. 95–97]'.

items.name: Remark 11.13 (the Breuil–Strauch conjecture in its original formulation)
items.statement: For the first cover Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D} (with Teitelbaum's semistable model over K = Q_{p²}((−p)^{1/(p²−1)}) [81] and the Hyodo–Kato cohomology of non-proper rigid spaces [48]), H^1_dR(Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D})^ρ = π^* ⊗ M_dR(π)^* compatibly with (φ, N, G_{Q_p})-structures (Saito [66]), and Breuil–Strauch's BS(ℒ), the dual of the preimage of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π^* in Ω^1(Σ_{1+ϖ_DO_D})^ρ, equals Π_ℒ^an for every admissible ℒ.
items.note: Argued via two global lines ℒ, ℒ′ from quaternionic forms and linearity of [BS(ℒ″)] and [Π_ℒ″^an] in Ext^1_G((O(Σ_n)^ρ)^*, π); relies on Remark 5.11.

items.name: Theorem 1.9 ((p, 0; 0, 1)-invariants of O(Σ_n)^ρ and Iwasawa cohomology)
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G with trivial central character, ρ = JL(π), n such that ρ is trivial on 1 + p^nO_D, and V = V(Π) for Π ∈ V(π) (the paper writes 'V ∈ V(π)'). Let D(Γ) be the algebra of L-valued distributions on Γ = Gal(Q_p^cyc/Q_p) ≅ Z_p^*. On the left-hand side below it acts through the action of (Z_p^*, 0; 0, 1) ≅ Γ. For m ≥ 0 let F_m = Q_p(µ_{p^m}), let ∫_{1+p^mZ_p} : H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗_L V) → H^1(G_{F_m}, V) be the natural maps, and let H^1_e(G_{F_m}, V) be the image of the Bloch–Kato exponential. Then there is an isomorphism of free D(Γ)-modules of rank 2: (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^{(p,0;0,1)=1} ≅ {µ ∈ H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗_L V) : ∫_{1+p^mZ_p} µ ∈ H^1_e(G_{F_m}, V) for all m ≥ 0}.
items.note: From Theorem 8.3 and Colmez [17, pp. 20, 174].

items.name: Theorem 1.10 (infinitely primitivable functions come from the half-plane)
items.statement: If f ∈ O(Σ_n) is infinitely primitivable, i.e. f ∈ ∩_{k≥0}(u^+)^k(O(Σ_n)) (in the image of (d/dz)^k for every k), then f ∈ O(Ω).
items.note: Decompose f along the ρ_i; for ρ_i nontrivial, O(Σ_n)^{ρ_i} = Π(π_i, 0)^* and ∩ Im((u^+)^j) = 0 on (Π^an)^* because u^+-power-torsion vectors are dense in Π^an for non-trianguline V ([31, th. 8.4.3]; alternatively injectivity of Res_{Z_p} [21], Remark 12.1).

items.name: Proposition 12.2 (the de Rham complex in the derived category of coadmissible D(G)-modules)
items.statement: With RΓ_dR(Σ_n) = [O(Σ_n) →^d Ω^1(Σ_n)] in D^b(D(G)) (coadmissible by Theorem 10.1) and its stupid filtration (F^0RΓ_dR = [0 → Ω^1(Σ_n)]), for every V ∈ V(π) and n large there is an isomorphism of filtered vector spaces, canonical up to scalar, Hom_{D^b(D(G))}((Π(V)^an)^*, RΓ_dR(Σ_n)^ρ[1]) = D_dR(V).
items.note: From Theorem 1.4 (the complex is split with H^1 = (Π(π, 2)^{u^+=0})^*); the level-0 analogue for the Steinberg (ρ = 1) is Schraen's theorem [74], refined to filtered (φ, N)-modules. Remark 12.3 records a hoped-for Hyodo–Kato refinement recovering V, a suggested argument of Scholze via Emerton's local–global compatibility and the p-adic Poincaré lemma [76, cor. 6.13], and the twisted complexes RΓ_dR(Σ_n, k).

items.name: Schneider–Teitelbaum: distribution algebras, Fréchet–Stein algebras and admissible locally analytic representations
items.statement: For a p-adic Lie group H, D(H) is the strong dual of LA(H), and for compact H it is a Fréchet–Stein algebra. Over a Fréchet–Stein algebra A: coadmissible modules form an abelian category; finitely presented (e.g. finitely generated projective) modules are coadmissible; A-linear maps between coadmissible modules have closed image; a finitely generated submodule of a coadmissible module is coadmissible (so finitely generated ideals are closed); and for M coadmissible and N ⊂ M a submodule, N is coadmissible ⟺ M/N is coadmissible ⟺ N is closed ([72, lemma 3.6]). Admissible locally analytic representations are those with coadmissible dual. For Π ∈ Ban^adm(G), Π^an is dense in Π. For a Stein space X, O(X) is a Fréchet–Stein algebra, and coadmissible O(X)-modules are the global sections of coherent sheaves on X.
items.note: Cited from Schneider–Teitelbaum [72]; PAPER-DING-25's brief plans the distribution algebra and the anti-equivalence with coadmissible modules.

items.name: Frommer's description of D_h(G_i)
items.statement: Let G_i = 1 + p^iM_2(Z_p), g_{i,1},…,g_{i,4} a minimal generating family and b_i^α = (g_{i,1} − 1)^{α_1}⋯(g_{i,4} − 1)^{α_4} ∈ Z_p[G_i] for α ∈ N^4. Elements of D(G_i) are uniquely Σ_α a_α b_i^α with a_α ∈ L and v_p(a_α) + r|α| → ∞ for every r > 0 (stated in the paper for G_2); D_h(G_i) is the completion of D(G_i) for ‖Σ a_α b_i^α‖_h = sup_α |a_α| p^{−|α|/p^h}. For 𝔤 = Lie(G_i) with basis X_1,…,X_4 and X^α = X_1^{α_1}⋯X_4^{α_4} ∈ U(𝔤), D_h(G_i) is a free module of finite type (left and right) over the closure U_h(𝔤) of U(𝔤) in D_h(G_i), with a basis of elements of Z_p[G_i], and the elements of U_h(𝔤) are uniquely Σ_α a_α X^α with v_p(a_α) − c_h|α| → ∞, where c_h depends only on h (the paper prints 'c_h > p^{h−1}'; see the source issue on p. 17: with this norm ‖X_j‖_h is about p^{h−1}, so c_h is about h − 1).
items.note: Cited from Frommer [44, 1.4, lemma 3, corollaries 1–3].

items.name: Lemma 5.9 (continuity of matrix-coefficient maps)
items.statement: For a locally analytic representation W of a p-adic Lie group G on a space of compact type and λ ∈ W^*, F : W → LA(G), w ↦ (g ↦ λ(g.w)), is continuous.
items.note: Via reflexivity and [70, prop. 3.2] (continuity of µ ↦ µ ∗ w).

items.name: Lemma 5.10 (weak and strong convergence of sequences)
items.statement: In a locally convex space over a spherically complete field, a sequence converges to 0 if and only if it converges weakly to 0.
items.note: Stated without proof.

items.name: ρ-isotypic parts, topological duals and L-coefficients of sheaves
items.statement: If V is a locally convex L-vector space, V^* is its topological dual; all duals in the paper are topological. For an L-representation σ of G × D^*, σ^ρ := Hom_{D^*}(ρ, σ), with the induced action of G. For a rigid analytic space X over Q_p and a coherent sheaf F on X, F(X) := H^0(X, F) ⊗_{Q_p} L. In particular O(X) = L ⊗_{Q_p} H^0(X, O_X) and Ω^1(X) = L ⊗_{Q_p} H^0(X, Ω^1_X), and the same convention applies to H^1_dR(X). De Rham cohomology is used only for smooth Stein rigid spaces. L is a finite extension of Q_p over which π and ρ are defined, enlarged as needed.
items.note: Théorèmes 1.2 and 1.4 cannot be stated without this: they use O(Σ_n)^ρ, Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ, H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ and (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^*. No existing item defines σ^ρ or the coefficient convention. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Subgroups of G, the basis of 𝔤𝔩_2 and the left-action convention
items.statement: G = GL_2(Q_p), G_0 = GL_2(Z_p), and G_n = 1 + p^nM_2(Z_p) for n ≥ 1. B is the upper-triangular Borel subgroup and P = (Q_p^*, Q_p; 0, 1) the mirabolic subgroup. 𝔤 = 𝔤𝔩_2 = Lie(G) has the basis a^+ = (1, 0; 0, 0), a^− = (0, 0; 0, 1), u^+ = (0, 1; 0, 0), u^− = (0, 0; 1, 0), and h = a^+ − a^− ∈ U(𝔤). All actions of G are on the left. When G acts on a rigid analytic space (or scheme) X, the natural right action on the global sections of a G-equivariant bundle on X becomes a left action via g ↦ g^{-1}. Thus (g.f)(z) = f(g^{-1}z) on O(Ω). a^+ and u^+ are the infinitesimal actions of (Z_p^*, 0; 0, 1) and (1, Z_p; 0, 1), and u^+ acts on O(Σ_n) as −d/dz.
items.note: Used by items 16, 43, 61–63, 79 and by Théorème 1.10 (u^+ = −d/dz). Check with this convention: a^+ − 1 = u^+ ∘ ∂ on O(Ω), with ∂ = multiplication by z (p. 8). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The quaternion division algebra D, its uniformizer and congruence subgroups
items.statement: D is the quaternion division algebra over Q_p, unique up to isomorphism. O_D is its unique maximal order, D_0 = O_D^*, and D_n = 1 + p^nO_D for n ≥ 1. An embedding Q_{p²} ↪ D is fixed once and for all. ϖ_D is a uniformizer of O_D such that O_D = Z_{p²}[ϖ_D], ϖ_D² = p, and ϖ_D x = σ(x)ϖ_D for all x ∈ Q_{p²}, where σ is the Frobenius of Q_{p²}.
items.note: Items 3, 9 and 10 use D, O_D and ϖ_D (for example X^un[ϖ_D^{2n−1}]), but none of them defines them. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Fields and Galois groups
items.statement: Q̄_p is a fixed algebraic closure of Q_p and C_p its completion; all extensions of Q_p are taken inside C_p. Q_{p²} is the unramified quadratic extension of Q_p, Q_p^nr the maximal unramified extension in Q̄_p, and Q̆_p its completion. For n ≥ 1, F_n = Q_p(µ_{p^n}), and Q_p^cyc is the completion of ∪_n F_n. G_{Q_p} = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p), H_{Q_p} = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p^cyc), and Γ = Gal(Q_p^cyc/Q_p), identified with Z_p^* by the cyclotomic character.
items.note: Used in item 35 onward (Γ, H_{Q_p}), in Théorème 1.9 (F_n) and throughout §§6–8 and 12. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 1.3(a): the trivial central character hypothesis is not essential
items.statement: The results of the paper remain valid for a supercuspidal π whose central character is not trivial, with ρ = JL(π); in particular this applies to Théorèmes 1.2 and 1.4. By contrast, the hypothesis that π is supercuspidal is essential (Remarque 1.5).
items.note: Asserted without proof. Item 84 covers only the other half of Remarque 1.3(a), the case π ⊗ Sym^k (Remarque 11.12). The proof of Théorème 1.10 (p. 66) applies Théorème 1.2 to every nontrivial constituent ρ_i of O(Σ_n), including those with nontrivial central character, so it rests on this remark (E40). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The G_i-stable Stein cover U_i = τ_n^{-1}(B_i) of Σ_n
items.statement: Let τ_n be the composite of Σ_n → Σ_0 with the retraction of Σ_0 onto the Bruhat–Tits tree of PGL_2(Q_p), whose origin is fixed at the standard lattice, and let B_i be the ball of radius i about the origin in the tree. Then the U_i = τ_n^{-1}(B_i) (i ≥ 0; n is implicit in the notation) form a Stein cover of Σ_n, and U_i is stable under G_i = 1 + p^iM_2(Z_p) for every i ≥ 1. Consequently O(Σ_n) = lim_i O(U_i).
items.note: Asserted without proof; footnote 23 points to this paragraph as the explanation of the standard fact that Ω is Stein (the case n = 0). Used in the proofs of Théorème 3.2 and Lemme 3.3 (U_{0,i} denotes the level-0 analogue). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Continuity of a group action lifted along a finite étale cover (Elkik, via Scholze)
items.statement: Since G_i acts continuously on O(U_{0,i}) and U_i → U_{0,i} is a G_i-equivariant finite étale morphism of affinoids, the action of G_i on O(U_i) is continuous; in particular g_n.f → f in O(U_i) when g_n → 1 in G_i.
items.note: Cited black box: 'la continuité de l'action de G_i, qui se déduit grâce au théorème d'Elkik — voir [77, lemma 2.5] — de l'énoncé analogue en niveau 0 et du fait que Σ_n → Σ_0 est un revêtement fini étale'. [77] = Scholze, On the p-adic cohomology of the Lubin–Tate tower. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 3.4 (local analyticity for coverings of Drinfeld spaces of any dimension)
items.statement: The argument proving Théorème 3.2 also applies to the coverings of Drinfeld's half-space in any dimension, using [73, Prop. 1] (Schneider–Teitelbaum, p-adic boundary values).
items.note: Side remark; not proved in detail and not used later. At present it is only mentioned in the note of /15. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 3.7 (H^1_dR,c of a Stein curve with a locally analytic action is smooth)
items.statement: If a p-adic Lie group G acts locally analytically on a smooth Stein analytic curve X, then H^1_dR,c(X) is a smooth G-module. The key point is the identity (𝔛.f)dg = (𝔛.g)df for analytic functions f, g on X and 𝔛 ∈ Lie(G) (in a local coordinate z both sides equal (∂f/∂z)(∂g/∂z)(𝔛.z)dz). It gives 𝔛.(f dg) = d(f·(𝔛.g)), which shows that 𝔛.Ω^1(X) ⊂ dO(X).
items.note: Split off from /17. Attributed to the referee. Checked: X.(f dg) = (X.f)dg + f d(X.g) = (X.g)df + f d(X.g) = d(f·X.g); since H^1_dR,c(X) = (Ω^1(X)/dO(X))^*, Lie(G) then acts by 0 on it. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 4.2(a) (de Rham cohomology of Ω computed without automorphic forms)
items.statement: The de Rham cohomology of Ω as a G-representation (even in any dimension) was computed by Schneider–Stuhler, de Shalit and Orlik [68, 78, 62] by various methods. Their proofs do not extend to higher level, but they have the merit of not using automorphic theory.
items.note: Cited results; not used in the proofs. At present it is only mentioned in the note of /22. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 4.2(b) (a local proof of Theorem 4.1 for the first covering)
items.statement: For the covering of the Drinfeld tower of level 1 + ϖ_D O_D, the computation of de Rham cohomology is much simpler because of an explicit formal model [81] (Teitelbaum; see [61], Pan, for details). In particular, for this covering Théorème 4.1 has a purely local proof, which moreover gives an isomorphism H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ π^* ⊕ π^*.
items.note: Cited results; not used in the proofs. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Lemma 4.4 (X is a finite union of Γ_i\G)
items.statement: The set B̄^*(Q)\B̄^*(A_f^p)/K^p is finite. Write B̄^*(A_f^p)/K^p = ∐_{i=1}^r B̄^*(Q)y_i and let Γ_i be the stabilizer of y_i in B̄^*(Q), viewed as a subgroup of G ≅ B̄^*(Q_p). Then Γ_i is discrete and cocompact in G, and there is an isomorphism of topological G-modules X = ∐_{i=1}^r Γ_i\G. In particular X is a compact p-adic analytic manifold on which G acts locally analytically.
items.note: Split off from /18. Its proof is left to the first reading ('standard'). Used in §4.2 (the y_i, Γ_i in the uniformization spectral sequence) and in §5.2 (proof of Théorème 5.7). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 4.5 (Hom_{K_p}(W^*, C^0(X)) ≅ A_{K_p}(W))
items.statement: For W ∈ Alg(G), let A_{K_p}(W) be the space of continuous functions f: X → W with f(xk) = k^{-1}.f(x) for all x ∈ X and k ∈ K_p (p-adic automorphic forms of weight W and level K^pK_p). There is a canonical isomorphism Hom_{K_p}(W^*, C^0(X)) ≅ A_{K_p}(W). Its inverse sends f ∈ A_{K_p}(W) to φ_f with φ_f(l)(x) = l(f(x)) for l ∈ W^* and x ∈ X.
items.note: Split off from /18. Proof: Hom_{K_p}(W^*, C^0(X)) ≅ ((W^*)^* ⊗_L C^0(X))^{K_p} ≅ (W ⊗_L C^0(X))^{K_p} ≅ C^0(X, W)^{K_p}; checked that K_p-invariance is f(xk) = k^{-1}.f(x). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 4.7 (automorphic description of K_p-algebraic vectors of C^0(X))
items.statement: Let W ∈ Alg(G) and ι: Q̄_p ≅ C. There is a canonical isomorphism Hom_{K_p}(W, C^0(X)) ⊗_{L,ι} C ≅ ⊕_π π_f^{K_pK^p}, the sum running over the automorphic representations π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f of B̄^*(A) with π_∞ ≅ W_∞. Hence C^0(X)_{K_p−alg} ⊗_{L,ι} C ≅ ⊕_{W∈Alg(G)} ⊕_{π_∞≅W_∞} W_∞ ⊗ π_f^{K_pK^p}. (The paper prints π_f^{K_p} in this last display: see the source issue on p. 22.)
items.note: Split off from /19. Deduced from Lemmes 4.5–4.6 by replacing W by W^*. Used in §4.2 (W trivial: lim_{K^p} LC(X(K^p))[π(f)^p] ≅ π), §5.1 (proof of Lemme 5.6) and §13 (Lemmes 13.8–13.9), where its G-equivariant form over all K_p (C^0(X)^alg ⊗ C ≅ ⊕_W ⊕_{π_∞≅W_∞} W_∞ ⊗ π_f^{K^p}) is used. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: The Shimura curve Sh_K attached to the indefinite quaternion algebra B
items.statement: Let B be a quaternion algebra over Q, split at ∞, of discriminant pℓ with ℓ ≠ p a fixed prime; fix B ⊗_Q Q_p ≅ D and a compact open K = K_p·K^p ⊂ B^*(A_f) with K_p = 1 + p^nO_D. Sh_K is the Shimura curve over Q classifying abelian surfaces with an action of O_B and level-K structure; Sh_K(C) = B^*(Q)\(X × B^*(A_f)/K), where B^*(Q) acts on X = C \ R through B^*(Q) → B^*(R) ≅ GL_2(R). It is regarded as a curve over Q_p (Sh_K for Sh_K ⊗_Q Q_p). B̄ is the quaternion algebra over Q isomorphic to B away from {p, ∞}, split at p and ramified at ∞, so B^*(A_f^p) ≅ B̄^*(A_f^p).
items.note: Used in Théorème 4.8, in the proof of Théorème 4.1 and in §5.2 (Théorème 5.7, which refers back to §§4.1–4.2 for its objects). Footnote 27: ℓ is fixed only to apply the results of §5.1 as they stand. The letter X here (C \ R) clashes with X = X(K^p) of Définition 4.3. Planned: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1 plans the quaternionic Shimura curves.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Galois coverings in de Rham cohomology (Schneider–Stuhler)
items.statement: For a Galois covering Y → Γ\Y of smooth rigid spaces whose group Γ acts freely (here Γ_i/p^{NZ} acting on M̆_{n,N}), there is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Γ, H^q_dR(Y)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_dR(Γ\Y).
items.note: Cited black box: 'La suite exacte de Hochschild-Serre [68, par. 5] pour le revêtement galoisien M̆_{n,N} → Γ_i\M̆_{n,N}'. [68] = Schneider–Stuhler, The cohomology of p-adic symmetric spaces. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: D^* acts on the geometric connected components of Σ_n through the reduced norm
items.statement: D^* acts on the set of geometrically connected components of Σ_n through the reduced norm. Consequently, since ρ = JL(π) is not one-dimensional, H^k_dR,c(Σ_{n,N})^{ρ^∨} = H^k_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨} vanishes for k ≠ 1.
items.note: Cited black box: deduced from Strauch [79] (for the Lubin–Tate tower) and the Faltings–Fargues isomorphism [36, 37]; the paper remarks that a simpler argument probably exists. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: The uniformization spectral sequence and its ρ-part (equations (2)–(3))
items.statement: Fix K^p ⊂ B̄^*(A_f^p) small enough and y_i, Γ_i as in Lemme 4.4. The choice of the y_i gives ∐_{i=1}^r Γ_i\M̆_n ≅ B̄^*(Q)\(M̆_n × B̄^*(A_f^p)/K^p). Let N be such that p^N ∈ Γ_i for all i, let M̆_{n,N} = p^{NZ}\M̆_n, and let Σ_{n,N} be the descent of p^{NZ}\M̆_n to Q_p via the Weil descent datum. Combining the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for M̆_{n,N} → Γ_i\M̆_{n,N}, Théorème 4.8 and its compatibility with Weil descent data, the algebraic duality between H^k_dR(Σ_{n,N}) and H^{2−k}_dR,c(Σ_{n,N}), the smoothness of H^{2−q}_dR,c(Σ_{n,N}) (trivial for q = 0, 2; Proposition 3.6 for q = 1), smooth Frobenius reciprocity and ∏_i Ind_{Γ_i}^G 1 = LC(X(K^p)), one obtains a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}(K^p) = Ext^p_G(H^{2−q}_dR,c(Σ_{n,N}), LC(X(K^p))) ⇒ H^{p+q}_dR(Sh_K). It does not depend on the choice of the y_i and is D^*-equivariant. Its ρ-part degenerates (only q = 1 survives) and gives an isomorphism (2) Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨}, LC(X(K^p))) ≅ H^1_dR(Sh_K)^ρ, compatible with change of the level K^p. This yields a B̄^*(A_f^p)-equivariant isomorphism (3) lim_{K^p} Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨}, LC(X(K^p))) ≅ lim_{K^p} H^1_dR(Sh_K)^ρ.
items.note: Numbered displays (2) and (3) in the proof of Théorème 4.1; at present they are only described in the note of /22. The independence of the y_i and the D^*-equivariance are 'checked as in' Fargues [38, prop. 4.3.11, lemmes 4.3.13–4.3.14]. The group in the E_2 term should be Γ_i/p^{NZ}, and the Ext groups should be taken for G/p^{NZ} (source issue on p. 23); only E_2^{0,1} is used. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: The π(f)^p-isotypic parts of both sides of (3)
items.statement: Let f be a quaternionic modular form of weight 2 for B̄^* whose automorphic representation π(f) of B̄^*(A) satisfies π(f)_p = π (it exists by Théorème 5.5); view π(f)^p as a representation of B^*(A_f^p) ≅ B̄^*(A_f^p). Then lim_{K^p} LC(X(K^p))[π(f)^p] ≅ π (Lemme 4.7 with W trivial) and lim_{K^p} H^1_dR(Sh_K)^ρ[π(f)^p] ≅ E with dim_L E = 2 ('théorèmes de comparaison standard'). Hence the π(f)^p-isotypic part of (3) reads Hom_G(H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨}, π) = E, which gives Théorème 4.1.
items.note: This implicitly uses (strong) multiplicity one for B̄^* and B^* (via the global Jacquet–Langlands correspondence /20), the transfer of π(f) to B^*(A) (its component at p being JL(π) = ρ), and the de Rham–Betti comparison with the automorphic decomposition of H^1 of the compact Shimura curve (each weight-2 π' contributes 2 dimensions). Footnote 29: for p > 2 a form attached to a Hecke character of an imaginary quadratic field would already suffice. Checked: the dimension count gives 2. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: The Hecke algebras T_Σ, T̃_Σ(K_p) and T̃_Σ
items.statement: Fix a finite set Σ = Σ(K^p) of primes containing p and the primes where K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ is ramified. For ℓ ∉ Σ the spherical Hecke algebra H(K_ℓ\B̄(Q_ℓ)^*/K_ℓ, O_L) is isomorphic to O_L[T_ℓ, S_ℓ^{±1}] (T_ℓ, resp. S_ℓ, the characteristic function of K_ℓ diag(ℓ, 1) K_ℓ, resp. K_ℓ diag(ℓ, ℓ) K_ℓ) and acts by continuous operators on C^0(X(K_p), M) and C^0(X, M) for every topological O_L-module M and every compact open subgroup K_p of G. Set T_Σ = ⊗′_{ℓ∉Σ} H(K_ℓ\B̄(Q_ℓ)^*/K_ℓ, O_L). For K_p compact open in B̄^*(Q_p), T̃_Σ(K_p) is the image of T_Σ in End_{O_L}(C^0(X(K_p), O_L)), a commutative O_L-algebra, free of finite type as an O_L-module; T̃_Σ = lim_← T̃_Σ(K_p) is the weak closure of the image of T_Σ in End^cont_{O_L}(C^0(X, O_L)), a compact, reduced, commutative O_L-algebra.
items.note: Asserted as standard. Split out of item 23. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Définition 5.2 b) (modular residual representations)
items.statement: A continuous representation r̄ : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(k_L) is modular (of tame level K^p) if it is associated (Définition 5.2 a)) with the canonical projection T̃_Σ → T̃_Σ/m for a maximal ideal m of T̃_Σ with residue field k_L.
items.note: Split out of item 23 (part b) of a two-part definition; merge back into item 23 if parts of a definition are kept together). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Définition 5.3 (the localized Hecke algebra A)
items.statement: Fix a modular r̄ : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(k_L) of tame level K^p, let m be the corresponding maximal ideal of T̃_Σ, and assume (Hypothèse) that r̄|G_{Q_p} is absolutely irreducible. A is the m-adic completion of T̃_Σ; it is a flat, local, noetherian, reduced O_L-algebra with residue field k_L, and a direct factor of T̃_Σ. For a T̃_Σ-module M, M_m = A ⊗_{T̃_Σ} M, a direct factor of M.
items.note: Split out of item 23. The properties of A are asserted without proof. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: The Galois representation r^m over A and the Banach representations Π(𝔭)
items.statement: Under the Hypothèse, r^m = lim_← r^m(K_p) : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(A), with r^m(K_p) : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(T̃_Σ(K_p)_m) given by Carayol's theorem, is associated with the canonical map T̃_Σ → A and reduces to r̄. For 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec(A[1/p]) (A[1/p] is a Jacobson ring) the residue field k(𝔭) is a finite extension of L and the image of A → k(𝔭) lies in its ring of integers; r(𝔭) : G_{Q,Σ} → GL_2(k(𝔭)) is the specialization of r^m along A[1/p] → k(𝔭), and Π(𝔭) is the unitary Banach representation of G attached to r(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} by the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for G.
items.note: Split out of item 23. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemme 5.6 (a quaternionic form with a prescribed Serre weight at p)
items.statement: Let σ be a minimal GL_2(Z_p)-type of π, σ_0 ⊂ σ a GL_2(Z_p)-stable lattice, σ̄_0 = σ_0 ⊗_{O_L} k_L, and W ∈ soc_{GL_2(Z_p)}(σ̄_0) a Serre weight. There is a quaternionic modular form g for B̄^* such that, if r : G_Q → GL_2(L) is the Galois representation attached to g, then (a) the restriction r̄_p := r̄|G_{Q_p} of the reduction r̄ : G_Q → GL_2(F̄_p) is absolutely irreducible, and (b) if π̄ is the smooth representation of G attached to r̄_p by the mod p local Langlands correspondence, then W ∈ soc_{GL_2(Z_p)}(π̄).
items.note: Stated inside the proof of Théorème 5.5; parts a) and b) are proved together. Proof: reduce to W = Sym^r F_p² (0 ≤ r ≤ p − 1); by the explicit mod p correspondence it suffices that r̄_p ≅ Ind_{Q_{p²}}^{Q_p} ω_2^{r+1} up to an unramified twist; take for g the Jacquet–Langlands transfer to B̄ of the weight-2 CM form attached to a Hecke character χ of an imaginary quadratic F in which p and the discriminant prime ℓ of §4.2 are inert, with χ_∞(z) = z^{-1}, prescribed reduction at p (misprinted η̄_p, issue E2) and χ_ℓ with Ind χ_ℓ supercuspidal. The proof gives g of weight 2. Split out of item 31. Missing: routed to route 5. Correction: η̄_p is a condition on the Galois character attached to χ, not on the local component of χ (E2).

items.name: Lemme 5.8 (Frobenius reciprocity for the uniformized Shimura curve)
items.statement: Write X = X(K^p) = ∐_{i=1}^r Γ_i\G (Lemme 4.4) and W = ((Ω^1(Σ_n))^ρ)^*, a locally analytic representation of G on a space of compact type (Théorème 3.2). There is an isomorphism of Hecke modules ⊕_{i=1}^r ((Ω^1(Σ_n))^ρ)^{Γ_i} ≅ Hom_G(W, LA(X)), sending ω = (ω_i)_i to φ_ω : ℓ ↦ (Γ_i g ↦ ℓ(g^{-1}.ω_i)); the inverse sends ψ to the r-tuple of elements of Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ = W^* given by ℓ ↦ ψ(ℓ)(Γ_i·1).
items.note: Continuity of φ_ω via Lemme 5.9. Split out of item 32. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Théorème 8.8 (Théorème 5.1 for Π(π, 0))
items.statement: There exists a nonzero continuous G-equivariant morphism Φ : Π(π, 0)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ.
items.note: The paper's reformulation of Théorème 5.1 through Définition 8.7 (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse ≅ Π(π, 0) for every V ∈ V(π), by Théorème 8.6). Split out of item 34. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The connection ∇ on (φ, Γ)-modules and the element t
items.statement: Let Δ be a (φ, Γ)-module over R. The action of Γ on Δ is differentiable (Berger [1, lemme 4.1]), which gives a connection ∇ : Δ → Δ, ∇(z) = lim_{a→1} (σ_a(z) − z)/(a − 1). For Δ = R, ∇ = t∂ with ∂ = (1 + T) d/dT and t = log(1 + T) ∈ R. Since φ(t) = pt and γ(t) = χ_cyc(γ)t for γ ∈ Γ, t^kΔ is again a (φ, Γ)-module over R for every integer k.
items.note: Split out of item 35. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Exemple 6.2 a) (the (φ, Γ)-module D_rig(V))
items.statement: Fontaine's theory [41] combined with the overconvergence theorem of Cherbonnier–Colmez [14] attaches to every L-representation V of G_{Q_p} an étale (φ, Γ)-module D_rig(V) over R of rank dim_L V, and (Berger [1]) the functor V ↦ D_rig(V) is fully faithful.
items.note: Split out of item 35 (Exemple 6.2 b) is item 36). Planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.2 plans the Robba realization D_rig(V).

items.name: Berger's models Δ^{]0,r_n]} and the modules Δ^+_dif,n
items.statement: Let Δ be a (φ, Γ)-module over R. (Berger [2, th. I.3.3]) For n large (depending on Δ) there is a unique sub-E^{]0,r_n]}-module Δ^{]0,r_n]} of Δ such that R ⊗_{E^{]0,r_n]}} Δ^{]0,r_n]} → Δ is an isomorphism and E^{]0,r_{n+1}]} ⊗_{E^{]0,r_n]}} Δ^{]0,r_n]} has a basis contained in φ(Δ^{]0,r_n]}) (for existence, take the E^{]0,r_n]}-span of a fixed basis of Δ); Δ^{]0,r_n]} is stable under Γ and ∇, and φ(Δ^{]0,r_n]}) ⊂ Δ^{]0,r_{n+1}]} for n large. Let L_n = L ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}) and φ^{-n} : E^{]0,r_n]} → L_n[[t]], f ↦ f(ζ_{p^n}e^{t/p^n} − 1), a Γ-equivariant injective ring map (n ≥ 1). For n large set Δ^+_dif,n = L_n[[t]] ⊗_{E^{]0,r_n]}} Δ^{]0,r_n]} and Δ^+_dif = lim_→ Δ^+_dif,n, with transition maps u ⊗ z ↦ u ⊗ φ(z) (u ∈ L_n[[t]] ⊂ L_{n+1}[[t]], z ∈ Δ^{]0,r_n]}).
