Then Δ^+_dif is a free L_∞[[t]] := lim_→ L_n[[t]]-module of the same rank as Δ, with a Γ-action preserving Δ^+_dif,n for n large, whose derivative is a connection ∇ on Δ^+_dif preserving Δ^+_dif,n for n large and satisfying ∇(fz) = t (df/dt)·z + f·∇z for f ∈ L_∞[[t]], z ∈ Δ^+_dif. For Δ = D_rig(V) one writes D^{]0,r_n]}(V), D^+_dif,n(V) (and N^{]0,r_n]}(V), N^+_dif,n(V) for N_rig(V)).
items.note: Split out of item 37. Missing: routed to route 6.

items.name: Colmez: no φ-eigenvector in D_rig(V) for non-trianguline V
items.statement: (As used from Colmez [19, lemme 3.2].) If V is an absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p} that is not trianguline, then φ has no eigenvector in D_rig(V), even after replacing L by a finite extension.
items.note: Cited result; split out of item 38. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Dospinescu: the kernel of P(∇) on D_rig(V) is finite-dimensional
items.statement: (Dospinescu [30, prop. 2.1], as used.) For P ∈ L[X] nonzero and V a 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p}, the kernel of P(∇) on D_rig(V) is a finite-dimensional L-vector space.
items.note: Cited black box; mentioned in the note of item 39 but has no item. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Schneider–Teitelbaum: continuity of μ ↦ μ ∗ w
items.statement: (Schneider–Teitelbaum [70, prop. 3.2], as used.) Let W be a locally analytic representation of a compact p-adic Lie group G on a space of compact type. For w ∈ W the map D(G) → W, μ ↦ μ ∗ w (= I(ρ_w)(μ)), is continuous, and λ(μ ∗ w) = ∫_G λ(g.w) dμ(g) for λ ∈ W^*.
items.note: Cited black box; item 89 covers other Schneider–Teitelbaum results but not this one. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Compatibility of p-adic local Langlands with reduction mod p
items.statement: Let V be a 2-dimensional L-representation of G_{Q_p} whose reduction V̄ is absolutely irreducible. Then the reduction mod p of (any open bounded G-stable lattice in) the Banach representation Π(V) attached to V by the p-adic local Langlands correspondence is the irreducible smooth representation π̄ attached to V̄ by the mod p local Langlands correspondence.
items.note: Used without reference in 'en réduisant mod p, on en déduit que π̄ = Π(𝔭)‾ se plonge dans C^0(X(K^p), k_L)[m]'. Standard (Berger–Breuil, Colmez [17]). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Hecke: weight-2 CM forms from imaginary quadratic Hecke characters
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary quadratic field and χ a Hecke character of F with χ_∞(z) = z^{-1} that does not factor through the norm. The global automorphic induction of χ is the automorphic representation of a cuspidal modular form of weight 2; at a prime ℓ inert in F its local component is the local automorphic induction Ind_{F_ℓ}^{Q_ℓ} χ_ℓ, and its p-adic Galois representation is the induction from G_F to G_Q of the p-adic Galois character attached to χ.
items.note: Used as 'La théorie de Hecke dit alors que...'; classical black box, combined with global Jacquet–Langlands (item 20). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: M_dR(π), the filtrations Fil_ℒ and (N_rig(π))^+_dif,n
items.statement: M_dR(π) = (Q̄_p ⊗_{Q_p^nr} M(π))^{G_{Q_p}} ≅ (K ⊗_{K_0} M(π)^{Gal(Q̄_p/K)})^{Gal(K/Q_p)} is a 2-dimensional L-vector space. The (φ, Γ)-module N_rig(π) of Définition 6.7 does not depend on K and is free of rank 2 over R, and for n large there is a canonical isomorphism (N_rig(π))^+_dif,n ≅ L_n[[t]] ⊗_L M_dR(π). Every L-line ℒ ⊂ M_dR(π) defines a decreasing exhaustive filtration Fil_ℒ on M_dR(π): Fil^{-1} = M_dR(π), Fil^0 = ℒ, Fil^1 = 0.
items.note: Split out of item 8 (M(π) itself is item 4). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The bijection V(π) ≅ Proj(M_dR(π))
items.statement: View V(π), via Colmez's functor [17] and [23], as a set of absolutely irreducible 2-dimensional L-representations of G_{Q_p}. For V ∈ V(π) an isomorphism of (φ, G_{Q_p})-modules D_pst(V) ≅ M(π) is unique up to scalar and induces D_dR(V) ≅ (Q̄_p ⊗_{Q_p^nr} D_pst(V))^{G_{Q_p}} ≅ M_dR(π); the Hodge line ℒ(V) = Fil^0 D_dR(V) ⊂ M_dR(π) does not depend on the choice. Conversely, for every L-line ℒ ⊂ M_dR(π) the filtration Fil_ℒ is weakly admissible (the Weil representation attached to M(π) is irreducible; cf. [8, proof of th. 5.2]), so the Colmez–Fontaine theorem gives a unique V_ℒ ∈ V(π) with ℒ(V_ℒ) = ℒ; with [23, th. 1.3] (which uses [33]), V ↦ ℒ(V) is a bijection V(π) → Proj(M_dR(π)), whose inverse is written ℒ ↦ Π_ℒ.
items.note: Split out of item 8; combines items 5 and 6. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The identifications (5) attached to V ∈ V(π)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π). A choice of isomorphism D_pst(V) ≅ M(π) induces: an isomorphism of (φ, Γ)-modules over R N_rig(V) ≅ N_rig(π) (5), which gives for n large an identification of L_n[[t]]-modules with semilinear Γ-action N^+_dif,n(V) ≅ L_n[[t]] ⊗_L M_dR(π); an isomorphism of filtered L-vector spaces D_dR(V) ≅ (M_dR(π), Fil_{ℒ(V)}); for n large, identifications D^+_dif,n(V) ≅ Fil^0(L_n((t)) ⊗ M_dR(π)) ≅ tN^+_dif,n(V) + L_n[[t]] ⊗_L ℒ(V); and inclusions of (φ, Γ)-modules tN_rig(π) ⊂ D_rig(V) ⊂ N_rig(π). These depend on the choice only up to scalar, so the line ℒ(V) ⊂ M_dR(π) and the images in N_rig(π) and in L_n[[t]] ⊗_L M_dR(π) are well defined.
items.note: Consequence of Exemple 6.5 and Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1. Split out of item 8. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Colmez's G-equivariant sheaf U ↦ D_rig(V) ⊠ U on P^1(Q_p)
items.statement: For every 2-dimensional L-representation V of G_{Q_p}, Colmez [17, ch. II, IV, V] constructs a G-equivariant sheaf U ↦ D_rig(V) ⊠ U on P^1(Q_p) (G acting by (a b; c d)·x = (ax + b)/(cx + d)) with D_rig(V) ⊠ Z_p = D_rig(V), on which the monoid P^+ = (Z_p − {0} Z_p; 0 1) (which stabilises Z_p) acts by (p^k a b; 0 1)z = (1 + T)^b·φ^k(σ_a(z)) for z ∈ D_rig(V), k ≥ 0, a ∈ Z_p^*, b ∈ Z_p (σ_a ∈ Γ with χ_cyc(σ_a) = a). The global sections D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 form an LF space with continuous G-action and central character δ_V = χ_cyc^{−1} det V (viewed as a character of Q_p^* by local class field theory). For U ⊂ P^1(Q_p) compact open, extension by zero identifies D_rig(V) ⊠ U with a subspace of D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1. With w = (0 1; 1 0), also writing w for the induced involution of D_rig(V) ⊠ Z_p^*, one has D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 = D_rig(V) + wD_rig(V), and z ↦ (Res_{Z_p}(z), Res_{Z_p}(wz)) identifies D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 with {(z_1, z_2) ∈ D_rig(V) × D_rig(V) : Res_{Z_p^*}(z_2) = w(Res_{Z_p^*}(z_1))}.
items.note: Split from item 42 (unnumbered setup of Théorème 7.1); cited from Colmez [17]. The action of (1 0; pZ_p 1) is 'très compliquée'. Same planned home as item 42 (Colmez's construction). Planned: PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.3 plans Colmez's construction, including the sheaf D_rig(V) ⊠ U.

items.name: Remark 7.2 a) ((Π(V)^an)^* is its own orthogonal when det V = χ_cyc)
items.statement: If det V = χ_cyc, then δ_V = 1 and V̌ ≅ V canonically; the exact sequence of Théorème 7.1 c) becomes 0 → (Π(V)^an)^* → D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 → Π(V)^an → 0, and (Π(V)^an)^* is its own orthogonal in D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 for the pairing { }_{P^1} : (D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1) × (D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1) → L.
items.note: Split from item 42; immediate from Théorème 7.1. Used throughout §§8–11 (e.g. in the proof of Théorème 8.6). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 7.2 b) (D(H) preserves D_rig ⊠ U when H stabilises U)
items.statement: If U is a compact open subset of P^1(Q_p) and H is a compact open subgroup of G stabilising U, then D_rig ⊠ U ⊂ D_rig ⊠ P^1 is stable under D(H) ⊂ D(G), and Res_U(λ·z) = λ·Res_U(z) for all z ∈ D_rig ⊠ P^1 and λ ∈ D(H).
items.note: Split from item 42; gives the gl_2-action on D_rig ⊠ Z_p = D_rig of §7.2 and the D(Γ)-linearity of Res_{Z_p} used in the proof of Théorème 8.3. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 7.5 ((1 − u)^k v has infinite slope)
items.statement: Let V be as in §7.3, v ∈ Π(V)^{P−fini} and n, k as in Définition 7.4 a) (so ((1 p^n; 0 1) − 1)^k v = 0). Then for every u ∈ (1 Q_p; 0 1), (1 − u)^k v ∈ Π(V)^{P−fini}_c. More precisely, writing u = (1 x; 0 1), any m ≥ −v_p(x) and N ≥ m + n satisfy (Σ_{i=0}^{p^N−1} (1 i; 0 1))^k ∘ (p^m 0; 0 1)(1 − u)^k v = 0.
items.note: Split from item 44. Proof left to the first reading ('un exercice amusant'); checked: conjugating by (p^m 0; 0 1) replaces u by (1 y; 0 1) with y = p^m x ∈ Z_p and v by v' killed by ((1 p^{m+n}; 0 1) − 1)^k; writing y = j + p^N y' (0 ≤ j < p^N), Σ_{i<p^N}(1 i; 0 1)·(1 − (1 y; 0 1)) lies in the ideal generated by 1 − (1 p^N; 0 1) and 1 − (1 p^N y'; 0 1), and a product of k such factors kills v' (by continuity (1 p^{m+n}z; 0 1)v' = Σ_{l<k} C(z, l)A^l v' with A = (1 p^{m+n}; 0 1) − 1). P-finiteness of (1 − u)^k v uses the P-stability of Proposition 7.6. Used with k = 1 (Théorème 7.11). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The spaces LP(Q_p^*, X)^Γ, LP_c(Q_p^*, X)^Γ and their P-action
items.statement: Let X be an L_∞[[t]]-module with a semilinear action of Γ (for the natural action of Γ on L_∞[[t]] = lim_n L_n[[t]]). LP(Q_p^*, X)^Γ is the space of functions φ : Q_p^* → X with compact support in Q_p such that φ(ax) = σ_a(φ(x)) for all x ∈ Q_p^* and a ∈ Z_p^*; LP_c(Q_p^*, X)^Γ is its subspace of functions vanishing near 0, and φ ↦ (φ(p^i))_{i∈Z} is an L-linear isomorphism LP_c(Q_p^*, X)^Γ ≅ ⊕_{i∈Z} X. The fixed compatible system (ζ_{p^n})_{n≥1} defines the locally constant additive character ε : Q_p → µ_{p^∞}, ε(b) = ζ_{p^n}^{p^n b} for n ≥ −v_p(b), and P acts on LP(Q_p^*, X)^Γ and LP_c(Q_p^*, X)^Γ by ((a b; 0 1)φ)(x) = ε(bx)e^{tbx}φ(ax).
items.note: Split from item 44. Checked: the formula preserves Γ-equivariance (σ_c(ε(bx)e^{tbx}) = ε(bcx)e^{tbcx}) and is an action of P. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 7.10 (N^+_dif/D^+_dif and the classical Kirillov model of π)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π). Since N^+_dif(V) = L_∞[[t]] ⊗_L D_dR(V) and D^+_dif(V) = tN^+_dif(V) + L_∞[[t]] ⊗_L Fil^0(D_dR(V)), there is a canonical Γ-equivariant isomorphism N^+_dif(V)/D^+_dif(V) ≅ L_∞ ⊗_L D_dR(V)/Fil^0(D_dR(V)). As Γ acts smoothly on the right-hand side, LP_c(Q_p^*, N^+_dif(V)/D^+_dif(V))^Γ is the space of locally constant functions φ : Q_p^* → L_∞ ⊗_L D_dR(V)/Fil^0(D_dR(V)) with compact support in Q_p^* such that φ(ax) = σ_a(φ(x)) for x ∈ Q_p^*, a ∈ Z_p^*. There is a natural isomorphism (Hilbert 90) LP_c(Q_p^*, L_∞ ⊗_L D_dR(V)/Fil^0(D_dR(V)))^Γ ⊗_L L_∞ ≅ LC_c(Q_p^*, L_∞ ⊗_L D_dR(V)/Fil^0(D_dR(V))), and the right-hand side, with its natural P-action defined using ε, is the usual Kirillov model of π ⊗_L L_∞.
items.note: Split from item 49. The Hilbert 90 isomorphism is Galois descent L_∞ ⊗_L L_∞ ≅ LC(Γ, L_∞) (checked). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Theorem 7.11 (Π(V)^lisse = vectors killed by u^+ and a^+)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π). Then Π(V)^lisse = {v ∈ Π(V)^an : u^+v = a^+v = 0} = Π(V)^{P−lisse}_c, and there is a canonical isomorphism of P-modules Π(V)^lisse ≅ LC_c(Q_p^*, N^+_dif(V)/D^+_dif(V))^Γ (the Γ-equivariant locally constant functions with compact support in Q_p^*; cf. Remarque 7.10).
items.note: Split from item 49. Proof: for v ∈ Π^an killed by u^+, a^+ and x ∈ Q_p, v_x = (1 x; 0 1)v − v ∈ Π^{P−lisse}_c (Remarque 7.5), so u^−v_x = 0 (Proposition 7.9); by u^−(1 x; 0 1) = (1 x; 0 1)(−x²u^+ + u^− − xh) and h = 2a^+ (trivial central character), u^−v ∈ Π^{(1 Q_p; 0 1)} = 0 ([29, lemme 7.1]); Π^lisse ⊂ Π^{P−lisse}_c because π is supercuspidal (vanishing Jacquet module) and by Remarque 7.5; the isomorphism then comes from Proposition 7.9. The identity for u^−(1 x; 0 1) was checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: No nonzero vector of Π(V) is fixed by (1 Q_p; 0 1) (Dospinescu [29, lemme 7.1])
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π) and Π = Π(V), the space Π^{(1 Q_p; 0 1)} of vectors of Π fixed by the unipotent subgroup (1 Q_p; 0 1) is 0.
items.note: Cited as a consequence of Dospinescu [29, lemme 7.1] ('c'est un résultat élémentaire'); used as a black box. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The Jacquet module of a supercuspidal representation vanishes
items.statement: If π is an irreducible supercuspidal smooth representation of G = GL_2(Q_p), every vector of π is a finite linear combination of vectors (1 − u)v with u ∈ (1 Q_p; 0 1) and v ∈ π.
items.note: Classical fact used as a black box (applied to Π(V)^lisse ≅ π). Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3 plans the supercuspidality criteria and the supercuspidal support.

items.name: Theorem 8.1 (Colmez: Π^an/Π^lisse is the same for all Π ∈ V(π))
items.statement: Let V_1, V_2 ∈ V(π). The choice of isomorphisms D_pst(V_1) ≅ M(π) and D_pst(V_2) ≅ M(π) induces an isomorphism of topological G-modules Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_1)^lisse ≅ Π(V_2)^an/Π(V_2)^lisse.
items.note: Split from item 57. Due to Colmez [17, 21]; the paper deduces it from Théorème 8.6 and the construction preceding it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 8.4 b) (tN_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 is G-stable)
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π), the subspace tN_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 of D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 is stable under the action of G.
items.note: Split from item 54. 'Conséquence formelle' of the stability of tN_rig(V) under P^+ = (Z_p∖{0} Z_p; 0 1) and of Proposition 8.4 a); previously proved by Colmez [17, ch. VI] and [21]. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Generation of (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0} by (1 − φ)(tN_rig(V))^{ψ=1} (attributed to Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao [52, prop. 4.3.8])
items.statement: (As used in the proof of Proposition 8.4 a).) For V ∈ V(π), (tN_rig(V))^{ψ=0} is generated as a D(Γ)-module by (1 − φ)(tN_rig(V))^{ψ=1}; the paper says this follows 'par exemple' from [52, prop. 4.3.8].
items.note: Black box from [52]. Read literally (D(Γ) the distribution algebra of Γ, p. 10) the statement is false (E24); a valid version needs a larger ring acting on ∆^{ψ=0} (e.g. the Robba ring of Γ) or a density statement. Prop. 8.4 a) itself is true (Colmez [17, ch. VI], [21]). Missing: routed to route 7. Correction: read over D(Γ) the generation is false; [52] gives it over the Robba ring of Γ (E24).

items.name: Colmez: Bloch–Kato description of the image of (tN_rig(π))^{ψ=1} ([17, pp. 20, 174])
items.statement: For V ∈ V(π), the D(Γ)-module {µ ∈ H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗_L V) : ∫_{1+p^nZ_p} µ ∈ H^1_e(G_{F_n}, V) for all n ≥ 0} (F_n = Q_p(µ_{p^n}), H^1_e the image of the Bloch–Kato exponential) is the image under 1 − φ of (tN_rig(π))^{ψ=1}.
items.note: Split from item 52 (its part (2)); cited from Colmez [17, pp. 20 and 174]. Its locator is in another reading's range; F should check the exact form (H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗ V) is usually identified with D_rig(V)^{ψ=1}, whereas (1 − φ)(tN_rig)^{ψ=1} lies in D_rig(V)^{ψ=0}; as abstract D(Γ)-modules the two sides are isomorphic, so Théorème 1.9 is not affected). Missing: routed to route 7.

items.name: Corollaire 9.3 (the cokernel of u^+ on Π(π, 0)^*)
items.statement: The operator u^+ has closed image on Π(π, 0)^*, and Π(π, 0)^*/u^+(Π(π, 0)^*) ≃ (Π(π, 0)^{u^+=0})^* (a nuclear Fréchet quotient, identified with the dual of the kernel through restriction of linear forms).
items.note: Split from item /60. Proof: Proposition 9.1 gives closedness; the quotient is nuclear Fréchet, hence reflexive, and its dual is Π(π, 0)^{u^+=0}. Used in the proof of Théorème 9.4 and later (§11). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemme 9.5 (a^+v + v is smooth when u^+v is)
items.statement: Let Π ∈ V(π) (as fixed at the start of §9) and let v ∈ Π^an with u^+v ∈ Π^lisse. Then v_1 := a^+v + v ∈ Π^lisse.
items.note: Split from item /61. Proof: u^+(a^+ + 1) = a^+u^+ gives u^+v_1 = 0. The vanishing Casimir (Théorème 7.3) gives u^−u^+v + a^+v + (a^+)²v = 0, hence a^+v_1 = 0. Conclude with Théorème 7.11 (Π^lisse = {v ∈ Π^an : u^+v = a^+v = 0}). Checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 9.6 b) (the relations on (Π^an)^*)
items.statement: For every Π ∈ V(π), the choice of an isomorphism Π(π, 0) ≃ Π^an/Π^lisse induces an inclusion 𝔤(Π^an)^* ⊂ Π(π, 0)^*, and as operators on (Π^an)^*: a^+ = ∂ ∘ u^+ and u^− = −∂a^+ = −∂²u^+.
items.note: Split from item /62. Proof: apply Théorème 9.4 to u^+l ∈ Π(π, 0)^* and use the injectivity of u^+ on (Π^an)^* (Proposition 9.1) and the zero infinitesimal character. Checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemme 9.8 (g∂g^{-1}(a − c∂) = d∂ − b)
items.statement: For g = (a, b; c, d) ∈ G there is an equality of operators on Π(π, 0)^*: g∂g^{-1}(a − c∂) = d∂ − b. Consequently (c·g∂g^{-1} + d)(a − c∂) = det g.
items.note: Split from item /63. Proof: with x = a − c∂ and y = d∂ − b, ∂u^+ − u^+∂ = 1 gives yu^+x − xu^+y = det g. Combine with (6) and the injectivity of gu^+g^{-1}. Checked. The consequence is stated on p. 48 in the proof of Théorème 9.7. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemme 9.11 (G-equivariance of the functions φ_{l,v})
items.statement: For all g = (a, b; c, d) ∈ G, l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*, v ∈ Π(π, 0) and x ∈ P^1(Q_p): φ_{l,v}(gx) = ((cx + d)/det g)·φ_{(c∂+d)g^{-1}l, g^{-1}v}(x).
items.note: Split from item /64. Proved by applying Théorème 9.7 twice, to g and to g^{-1}; each step of the displayed chain checked. The proof, and the use in Proposition 9.10, concern x ∈ Q_p with cx + d ≠ 0. At x = −d/c both sides vanish, and at x = ∞ the right-hand side must be read as a limit. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Radius-of-analyticity filtration of Π(π, 0) (Colmez–Dospinescu [24, ch. IV])
items.statement: Writing Π(π, 0) = Π^an/Π^lisse and filtering Π by radius of analyticity, Π(π, 0) is an increasing union of Banach spaces Π(π, 0)^{(h)} (h ∈ N^*), each stable under (1, Z_p; 0, 1) but not under ∂ or ∂^{-1}. For every h there is M such that, if v'_n → 0 in Π(π, 0)^{(h)} and l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*, the functions x ↦ l((1, x; 0, 1)v'_n) tend to 0 in the space of analytic functions on a + p^M Z_p for every a ∈ Z_p ([24, th. IV.6, rem. IV.15]).
items.note: Cited black box. The filtration part is already in item /47 (another reading's file). Only the uniform-analyticity consequence [24, th. IV.6, rem. IV.15] as used here is new. Drop this entry if /47 is judged to cover it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The subspace S ⊂ O(Ω) and the measures µ_f
items.statement: S = Vect_{x∈Q_p} 1/(z − x) ⊂ O(Ω). For f ∈ S, µ_f ∈ (St^an)^* is the element corresponding to f under O(Ω) ≃ (St^an)^* (Proposition 9.12); explicitly µ_f = Σ_{x∈Q_p} a_x δ_x − (Σ_{x∈Q_p} a_x) δ_∞ if f = Σ a_x/(z − x). S is dense in O(Ω), by Proposition 9.12 and Hahn–Banach. For general f ∈ O(Ω), µ_f denotes the element of (St^an)^* corresponding to f.
items.note: Split from item /65. Used in Définition 9.13, Propositions 9.14–9.15, Théorème 9.9 and Proposition 9.16. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Proposition 9.14 (T_f for f ∈ O(Ω) as a limit)
items.statement: Let f ∈ O(Ω) and let (f_n) be a sequence in S converging to f in O(Ω). Then the operators T_{f_n} converge weakly, that is T_{f_n}(l) converges in Π(π, 0)^* for every l, to a continuous operator T_f : Π(π, 0)^* → Π(π, 0)^*.
items.note: Split from item /66. Proof: g_n = f_n − f_{n−1} → 0, so µ_{g_n} → 0 (Morita). By (7), ⟨T_{g_n}(l), v⟩ → 0, hence T_{g_n}(l) → 0 (Lemme 5.10 and reflexivity of Π(π, 0)). Ultrametric Cauchy plus completeness gives convergence, and Banach–Steinhaus gives continuity. Independence of the sequence follows from Proposition 9.15 a). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 9.15 a) (integral formula for T_f)
items.statement: For all f ∈ O(Ω), l ∈ Π(π, 0)^* and v ∈ Π(π, 0): ⟨T_f(l), v⟩ = ∫_{P^1(Q_p)} φ_{l,v} µ_f.
items.note: Split from item /66. Proof: pass to the limit in (7), using that µ_{f_n} converges weakly to µ_f (Morita duality). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 9.15 b) (continuity of f ↦ T_f(l))
items.statement: If f_n ∈ O(Ω) tends to f ∈ O(Ω), then lim_{n→∞} T_{f_n}(l) = T_f(l) in Π(π, 0)^* for every l ∈ Π(π, 0)^*.
items.note: Split from item /66. Proof: Lemme 5.10, part a) and Morita duality. The printed proof has a misprint (« v ∈ Π(π, 0)^* », E28). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Π(π, 0)^* is a locally free O(Ω)-module of rank dim_L ρ
items.statement: As a corollary of the final result, Π(π, 0)^* is locally free of rank dim_L(ρ) as an O(Ω)-module.
items.note: Split from item /67; p. 9 is in another reading's range. It follows from the O(Ω)-linear isomorphism Π(π, 0)^* ≃ O(Σ_n)^ρ (Théorème 1.2, Proposition 9.16) and the projectivity of O(Σ_n)^ρ (footnote 50, [56, prop. A5]). §9–§10 do not discuss the rank. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Kohlhaase: O(Σ_n) is a finitely generated projective O(Ω)-module
items.statement: O(Σ_n) is a finitely generated projective O(Ω)-module ([56, prop. A5]). Hence O(Σ_n)^ρ, a direct summand of O(Σ_n) as an O(Ω)-module, is finitely generated projective.
items.locator: §10.2, footnote 50, p. 57; §10.1, proof of Proposition 10.3, p. 52
items.note: Split from item /71; a cited black box. Used for N = O(Σ_n)^ρ in Proposition 10.11 (proof of Théorème 10.1). After base change to Q̆_p it gives the coadmissibility of O(M̆_n)^ρ over O(Ω̆) in the proof of Proposition 10.3. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Coadmissibility of O(Σ_n)^ρ and O(Σ_n) as D(G)-modules
items.statement: The D(G)-module O(Σ_n)^ρ is coadmissible. Decomposing O(Σ_n) under the action of D^*, the D(G)-module O(Σ_n) is coadmissible.
items.note: Split from item /74. Deduced from Théorème 10.1, Théorème 8.8 and [72, lemma 3.6]: O(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ Π(π, 0)^*/ker Φ with ker Φ closed. For the claim about all of O(Σ_n), see E30. Not used later. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 10.8 (topological irreducibility of O(Σ_n)^ρ as an equivariant O(Ω)-module)
items.statement: The O(Ω)-module O(Σ_n)^ρ, with its semilinear action of G, is topologically irreducible: every nonzero closed G-stable O(Ω)-submodule of O(Σ_n)^ρ is the whole space.
items.note: Split from item /72. Proof: V ≠ 0 implies V̆ ≠ 0. The proof of Proposition 10.3 shows that O(Σ̆_n)^ρ is irreducible as an equivariant O(Ω̆)-module, so V̆ has dense image, and Lemme 10.2 gives V dense, hence V is everything. Remark 10.9: irreducibility as a topological G-module (without O(Ω)) is not proved here, but holds by [21] and Théorème 1.2. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Proposition 10.10 (equivariant O(Ω)-linear endomorphisms of O(Σ_n)^ρ are scalar)
items.statement: Every O(Ω)-linear G-equivariant endomorphism of O(Σ_n)^ρ is scalar.
items.note: Split from item /72. Proof: extend scalars to Q̆_p and use Kohlhaase's equivalence (Théorème 10.5) together with the fact that D^*-equivariant endomorphisms of ρ^* ⊗ O_{P̆^1} are scalar, by twisting by O(λ) as in the proof of Proposition 10.3. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Proposition 11.1 (Π(π, 2)^* and the differential d)
items.statement: Π(π, 2)^* is a representation of G, and the map d : Π(π, 0)^* → Π(π, 2)^*, d(l) = −u^+(l) dz, is G-equivariant with closed image.
items.note: Split from item /75. Its proof was not checked in this review. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The isomorphisms α_dif, α_{P^1}, ξ_{V,α} and the embedding ι_{V,α}
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π) and α : D_pst(V) ≃ M(π). Then α induces Γ-isomorphisms α_dif : N^+_dif(V) ≃ L_∞[[t]] ⊗_L M_dR(π) and α_dif : t^{-1}N^+_dif(V)/N^+_dif(V) ≃ L_∞(−1) ⊗_L M_dR(π). Through tN_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 ≃ tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 it also induces an isomorphism α_{P^1} : (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^* → Π(π,0)^*. The isomorphism ξ_{V,α} : Π(π,0) ≃ Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse is the transpose of α_{P^1} composed with [(Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^*]^* ≃ Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse. Finally ι_{V,α} = α_dif ∘ Ψ_V ∘ (ξ_{V,α}|_{Π(π,0)^{u^+=0}}) : Π(π,0)^{u^+=0} → LP(Q_p^*, L_∞(−1) ⊗_L M_dR(π))^Γ. Replacing α by xα (x ∈ L^*) replaces ξ_{V,α} by xξ_{V,α} and ι_{V,α} by x²ι_{V,α}.
items.note: The paper prints the target of ι_{V,α} as LC(Q_p^*, L_∞(−1) ⊗_L M_dR(π)); see E34. I checked the scaling x² (α_dif and ξ are both linear in α). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The maps i_{j,n} on Π(π,0)^* and the pairing { }_{dif,V}
items.statement: Π(π,0)^* ⊂ tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1, and even Π(π,0)^* ⊂ tN^{]0,r_n]} ⊠ P^1 for n large enough (depending only on V). For such n and j ∈ Z, i_{j,n} = φ^{-n} ∘ Res_{Z_p} ∘ (p^{n−j}, 0; 0, 1) : Π(π,0)^* → t(N_rig(π))^+_dif = tL_∞[[t]] ⊗_L M_dR(π). If l ∈ (Π(V)^an/Π(V)^lisse)^* and L = α_{P^1}(l), then i_{j,n}(L) = α_dif(i_{j,n}(l)), where i_{j,n}(l) is the map of §7.4. { }_{dif,V} is the pairing between tN^+_dif(V) and t^{-1}N^+_dif(V)/N^+_dif(V) induced by the pairing { }_dif between D_dif(V̌)^+[1/t] = D_dif(V)^+[1/t] and D_dif(V)^+[1/t].
items.note: Used in Lemmes 11.4–11.5. The fixed radius r_n (from [24, cor. VI.13], p. 38) is also what makes the t-divisibility step in Proposition 11.10 work (see E38). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 11.4 (the duality formula for Π(π,0) in the Kirillov model)
items.statement: Let V ∈ V(π) and α : D_pst(V) ≃ M(π). Let Π(π,0)^{u^+=0}_c be the subspace of Π(π,0)^{u^+=0} spanned by the (1 − n)v with n ∈ (1, Q_p; 0, 1) and v ∈ Π(π,0)^{u^+=0}. If L ∈ Π(π,0)^* and v ∈ Π(π,0)^{u^+=0}_c, then for every n large enough L(v) = Σ_{j∈Z} {α_dif^{-1}(i_{j,n}(L)), α_dif^{-1}(ι_{V,α}(v))(p^{-j})}_{dif,V}.
items.note: Proof: write L = α_{P^1}(l); v_1 = ξ_{V,α}(v) lies in Π(V)^{P−fini}_c/Π(V)^lisse (Remarque 7.5 with k = 1); then Théorème 7.8. The last line prints i_{V,α} for ι_{V,α} (E3). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 11.5 (non-degeneracy of the Kirillov pairing)
items.statement: Let V_1 ∈ V(π) and α_1 : D_pst(V_1) ≃ M(π). Let (x_j)_{j∈Z} be a finitely supported sequence of elements of t^{-1}N^+_dif(V_1)/N^+_dif(V_1) such that, for every L ∈ Π(π,0)^* and every n large enough, Σ_{j∈Z} {α_{1,dif}^{-1}(i_{j,n}(L)), x_j}_{dif,V_1} = 0. Then x_j = 0 for all j.
items.note: Proof: Proposition 7.6 gives v ∈ Π(V_1)^{P−fini}_c with φ_v(p^{-j}) lifting x_j (to t^{-1}N^+/D^+ ⊂ D^-_dif; the lift does not matter since tN^+ ⊥ N^+ by Proposition 7.7(b)). Théorème 7.8 gives l(v) = 0 for all l ∈ (Π(V_1)^an/Π(V_1)^lisse)^*, so v ∈ Π(V_1)^lisse, and one concludes by Théorème 7.11 and Proposition 7.9. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 11.8 (separate local analyticity of orbit maps on Π(π,2)) and the 𝔤-action on Π(π,2)
items.statement: For every v ∈ Π(π,2), the map f_v : (a, b, c, d) ↦ (a, b; c, d).v is locally analytic in each of the variables a, b, c, d separately, near (1, 0, 0, 1). Consequently, on Π(π,2), a^+ = ∂u^+, a^− = −∂u^+ and u^− = −∂²u^+. So a vector killed by u^+ is killed by 𝔤, and Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} is a smooth representation of G.
items.note: Proof: as B-representations Π(π,2) and Π(π,0) differ by a character, and f_v(1,0,x,1) = w f_{w.v}(1,x,0,1). The paper does not define ∂ on Π(π,2); read as the transpose of ∂ on Π(π,2)^* = Π(π,0)^* dz, the formulas check. From (10) and Proposition 9.6 one gets on Π(π,2)^*: a^+ = u^+∂, a^− = −u^+∂, u^− = −u^+∂², and dualizing gives the stated formulas. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 11.11 (∩_j Im((u^+)^j) = 0 on Π(π,0)^*)
items.statement: The intersection of the Im((u^+)^j), j ≥ 0, on Π(π,0)^* (or on Π(π,2)^*) is zero. This is shown in the proof of Théorème 1.10 using a delicate result of [31]; the proof of Proposition 11.10 avoids it.
items.note: Proved in §12.1, p. 66, from [31, th. 8.4.3] (density in Π^an of the vectors killed by a power of u^+ when V is non-trianguline). Alternative: Remarque 12.1. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 12.1 (alternative via the injectivity of Res_{Z_p}, Colmez [21])
items.statement: An element z of the intersection of the Im((u^+)^j), viewed in D_rig ⊠ P^1, satisfies Res_{Z_p}(z) = 0. So instead of [31] one could use the injectivity, proved by Colmez [21], of Res_{Z_p} : (Π^an)^* → D_rig.
items.note: Uses Colmez [21] (injectivity of Res_{Z_p} on (Π^an)^*) as a black box. 'Trivialement' rests on the same t-divisibility argument as Proposition 11.10: it needs a fixed radius of convergence (see E38). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 12.3 (Hyodo–Kato refinement, Scholze's suggestion, twisted de Rham complexes)
items.statement: (a) A more satisfying result would replace the de Rham complex by a log-rigid cohomology complex and give a canonical isomorphism of filtered (φ, N, G_{Q_p})-modules between the left side of Proposition 12.2 and D_pst(V), which would recover V from Π(V)^an. (b) Proposition 12.2 is much weaker than the Breuil–Strauch conjecture. For V ∈ V(π) of global origin, P. Scholze indicated an argument deducing it from Emerton's local–global compatibility and the p-adic Poincaré lemma [76, cor. 6.13]. (c) For k ∈ Z and n ≥ 0, RΓ_dR(Σ_n, k) = RΓ_dR(Σ_n) ⊗ (Sym^k)^* = [O(Σ_n) ⊗ (Sym^k)^* →^{d⊗id} Ω^1(Σ_n) ⊗ (Sym^k)^*]. It can be filtered as in [68, pp. 95–97], with F^iRΓ_dR(Σ_n, k) = RΓ_dR(Σ_n, k) for i < −k, 0 for i > 0, and [0 → O(k+2)(Σ_n) ⊗ det^{k+1}] for −k ≤ i ≤ 0. One could then prove the exact analogue of Proposition 12.2 for Hodge–Tate weights 0, k+1.
items.note: Speculative. (c) is asserted without proof ('on pourrait prouver'), like Remarque 11.12. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 13.3 (the module M and its Schikhof dual M^*)
items.statement: M = Hom^cont_{A[G]}(Π^univ, C^0(X, O_L)_𝔪), where Π^univ has the 𝔪-adic topology and C^0(X, O_L)_𝔪 the topology induced by C^0(X, O_L). M is a flat O_L-module, separated and complete for the p-adic topology. M^* = Hom_{O_L}(M, O_L) is its Schikhof dual, with the topology of pointwise convergence; conversely M = Hom^cont_{O_L}(M^*, O_L).
items.note: Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Remark 13.4 (fibres of M)
items.statement: For every 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec(A[1/p]) there are canonical isomorphisms M[𝔭][1/p] = k(𝔭) ⊗_{A/𝔭} M[𝔭] ≃ Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) ≃ Hom^cont_{A[G]}(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)_𝔪).
items.note: Stated as immediate (uses Π^univ ⊗_A k(𝔭) ≃ Π(𝔭)). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 13.2 (density of GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors)
items.statement: If ℬ is a topological direct factor (as a G-module) of C^0(X), then the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors ℬ_{GL_2(Z_p)−alg} are dense in ℬ.
items.note: Reduced to ℬ = C^0(X). It then follows from Lemme 13.1 and Mahler's theorem (polynomial functions are dense in C^0(GL_2(Z_p), L)); the paper refers to [63, prop. A.3] and [23, prop. 2.12] for general results. Split from item 26. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 13.6 (M^* is finitely generated)
items.statement: The A-module M^* is finitely generated.
items.note: M^* is compact, so it suffices that M^*/𝔪M^* is finite-dimensional over k_L. Its dual (M/π_LM)[𝔪] embeds in Hom_{k_L[G]}(π̄, LC(X, k_L)_𝔪) ⊂ LC(X(K_p), k_L), which is finite-dimensional because π̄ is smooth irreducible. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 13.7 (fibres of M and support of M^*)
items.statement: If 𝔭 is a maximal ideal of A[1/p], then M[𝔭][1/p] is a finite-dimensional L-vector space, dual to M^* ⊗_A k(𝔭), and it is nonzero if and only if 𝔭 ∈ Supp M^*[1/p].
items.note: Proof via Lemme 13.6 and Nakayama. Supp M^*[1/p] is closed since M^*[1/p] is finitely generated. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: The family 𝒞 of classical crystalline points of Spec A[1/p]
items.statement: Let σ be an automorphic representation of B̄^*(A) such that (a) σ is unramified outside Σ, (b) σ_f^{K^p} ≠ 0 and σ_p^{GL_2(Z_p)} ≠ 0, (c) the associated Galois representation r_σ satisfies r̄_σ = r̄. The action of T̃_Σ on σ_f defines T̃_Σ → L, which extends by continuity to A[1/p] → L (since r̄_σ = r̄); its kernel is a maximal ideal 𝔭_σ of A[1/p]. 𝒞 = {𝔭_σ : σ as above}. LP(X) denotes the space of locally algebraic vectors of C^0(X)_𝔪.
items.note: The eigenvalues of σ may need a finite extension of L (tacitly enlarge L). The points of 𝒞 are crystalline at p because σ_p^{GL_2(Z_p)} ≠ 0. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 13.8 (𝒞 is Zariski dense)
items.statement: The set 𝒞 is Zariski dense in Spec A[1/p].
items.note: A[1/p] is reduced and acts faithfully on C^0(X)_𝔪. By Lemme 13.2 the GL_2(Z_p)-algebraic vectors are dense, and by Lemme 4.7 they lie in Σ_{𝔭∈𝒞} C^0(X)_𝔪[𝔭]. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Lemma 13.9 (the classical points lie in the support)
items.statement: For every 𝔭 ∈ 𝒞, M[𝔭] ⊗_{A/𝔭} k(𝔭) ≠ 0, i.e. Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) ≠ 0. Moreover LP(X)[𝔭] is contained in the image of the natural map Π(𝔭) ⊗ Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), C^0(X)[𝔭]) → C^0(X)[𝔭].
items.note: r(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} is crystalline and absolutely irreducible, with HT weights a < b; W = Sym^{b−a−1}(L²) ⊗ det^a. By Berger–Breuil [3], Π(𝔭) is the universal unitary completion of σ_p ⊗ W. Lemme 4.7 then gives (σ_p ⊗ W) ⊗ Hom_G(σ_p ⊗ W, LP(X)[𝔭]) ≃ LP(X)[𝔭]. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Berger–Breuil: universal unitary completions of crystalline locally algebraic representations
items.statement: If r(𝔭)|G_{Q_p} is crystalline and absolutely irreducible with Hodge–Tate weights a < b, σ_p is the associated unramified smooth representation and W = Sym^{b−a−1}(L²) ⊗ det^a, then the universal unitary completion of the locally algebraic representation σ_p ⊗ W is Π(𝔭). Hence Hom^cont_G(Π(𝔭), B) = Hom_G(σ_p ⊗ W, B) for every unitary Banach representation B, and σ_p ⊗ W ⊂ Π(𝔭).
items.note: Cited: Berger–Breuil [3], together with the construction of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence. Black box used in Lemme 13.9. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Emerton [33]: completed tensor products with admissible orthonormalizable A[G]-modules
items.statement: As used for Théorème 5.4 (with M^* finitely generated over A and Π^univ an admissible orthonormalizable A[G]-module): (i) [33, Lemma 3.1.16] Π^univ ⊗̂_A M is π_L-adically separated; (ii) [33, Prop. 3.1.3 with Lemma 3.1.16] the image of the evaluation map (Π^univ ⊗̂_A M)[1/p] → C^0(X)_𝔪 is closed; (iii) [33, Lemma B.6] (Π^univ/π_L ⊗_A M/π_L)[𝔪] ≃ Hom_A(A/𝔪, M/π_L) ⊗_{A/π_L} Π^univ/π_L; (iv) [33, Lemma 3.1.17] (Π^univ ⊗̂_A M)[1/p][𝔭] = Hom_A(A/𝔭, M) ⊗̂_A Π^univ[1/p] for 𝔭 ∈ MaxSpec(A[1/p]).
items.note: Cited from Emerton's preprint [33]. I did not check the numbering of [33]; the statements are as the proof uses them. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Dospinescu [31, th. 8.4.3]: density of u^+-power-torsion vectors
items.statement: For Π ∈ V(π) (more generally when the Galois representation is not trianguline), the subspace of Π^an of vectors killed by a power of u^+ is dense in Π^an; this property is equivalent to V being non-trianguline. Consequently ∩_j Im((u^+)^j) = 0 on (Π^an)^*.
items.note: Cited from Dospinescu's thesis [31]. Black box in the proof of Théorème 1.10 and behind Remarque 11.11 (alternative: Remarque 12.1 with [21]). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Kirillov model of a supercuspidal representation
items.statement: For π supercuspidal, π = π_c (the span of the (1 − n)v, n ∈ (1, Q_p; 0, 1)). π_c and LC_c(Q_p^*, L_∞)^Γ are isomorphic as P-representations and irreducible, and the usual Kirillov model gives a P-equivariant isomorphism π ⊗ M_dR(π) ≃ LC_c(Q_p^*, L_∞ ⊗_L M_dR(π))^Γ (P acting through the additive character ε). There is no nonzero (1, Q_p; 0, 1)-invariant vector in LC(Q_p^*, L_∞)^Γ.
items.note: 'Résultat standard de la théorie du modèle de Kirillov des représentations supercuspidales'. Black box in Théorème 11.7; End_P(π) = L is also used to make the P-isomorphism G-equivariant. Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: Supercuspidal representations are projective
items.statement: A supercuspidal representation π of G with trivial central character is a projective object of the category of smooth representations of G with trivial central character. In particular a G-equivariant surjection from a smooth representation (with trivial central character) onto π^{⊕2} splits.
items.locator: §11.2, proof of Théorème 11.7, p. 62; §11.3, footnote 52, p. 64
items.note: Standard fact, used to split Π(π,2)^{u^+=0} ↠ π^{⊕2} (Théorème 11.7) and, in footnote 52, to turn the quotient π^{⊕2} of H^1_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ^∨} (Théorème 4.1) into a sub-object (Proposition 11.10). Missing: routed to route 9.

items.name: The boundary sheaf F_π on P^1(Q_p) (§12.3)
items.statement: Let τ_n be the composite of the canonical surjection Σ_n → Σ_0 with the retraction of the half-plane onto the Bruhat–Tits tree (with its standard origin), and B_i the ball of radius i around the origin. For an open U ⊂ P^1(Q_p), let V be the open subset of the tree formed by all half-lines from the origin ending at a point of U, and set F_π(U) = lim_{→ i} O(τ_n^{-1}(V − B_i))^ρ. This defines a sheaf F_π on P^1(Q_p), a sheaf of sections of the structure sheaf 'at the boundary' of Σ_n.
items.note: Conjecture 12.4 (not proved): F_π is Colmez's sheaf U ↦ tN_rig(π) ⊠ U (item 56), and the exact sequence 0 → Π(π,0)^* → tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1(Q_p) → Π(π,2) → 0 of [21] is identified with the sequence 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → F_π(P^1(Q_p)) → (Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ)^* → 0 deduced from (11): 0 → O(Σ_n) → lim_{→Z} O(Σ_n − Z) → H^1_c(Σ_n, O) → 0 and Serre duality Ω^1(Σ_n)^* ≃ H^1_c(Σ_n, O) [13]. Not on the way to the main results; included because Conjecture 12.4 is the paper's numbered statement in §12.3. Missing: routed to route 1.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, Correspondance de Langlands locale p-adique et changement de poids, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 21 (2019), 797–838
prerequisites.why: The source of Π(π, 0), the operator ∂ and its existence (Théorème 9.4), the independence of Π^an/Π^lisse (Théorèmes 8.5–8.6) and the irreducibility of Π(π, 0) (Remarque 1.8); the paper reproves several of its results.

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, G. Dospinescu, Complétés universels de représentations de GL_2(Q_p), Algebra Number Theory 8 (2014), 1447–1519
prerequisites.why: Π^an determines Π, the factorization of (Π^an)^* through D^{]0,r_m]} ⊠ P^1 and the filtration by radius of analyticity (§§7.4, 9.2, 11.2).

prerequisites.citation: P. Colmez, G. Dospinescu, V. Paškūnas, The p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p), Camb. J. Math. 2 (2014), 1–47
prerequisites.why: The bijection between V(π) and the potentially crystalline representations with D_pst ≅ M(π) (§1.1, Exemple 6.6).

prerequisites.citation: G. Dospinescu, Actions infinitésimales dans la correspondance de Langlands locale p-adique, Math. Ann. 354 (2012), 627–657
prerequisites.why: Théorème 7.3 and the smooth vectors of Proposition 7.9.

routes.title: P-adic local Langlands for GL₂(Q_p), Part II: the geometric realisation in the Drinfeld tower
routes.brief:
This route coalesces with PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2QpPartIIGeometricRealisation, proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B and extended by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Dospinescu–Le Bras, 'Revêtements du demi-plan de Drinfeld et correspondance de Langlands p-adique' (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), 321–411; arXiv:1509.00606), is the de Rham layer of that roadmap: the Breuil–Strauch conjecture that PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B quotes as its Proposition 2.9 is proved here.

Final theorems, as the paper states them (π supercuspidal of GL_2(Q_p) with trivial central character, ρ = JL(π), n with ρ trivial on 1 + p^nO_D). Theorem 1.2: for every Π ∈ V(π) there is an isomorphism of topological G-modules, unique up to scalar, (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^* ≅ Π^an/Π^lisse. Theorem 1.4: there is a canonical (up to scalar) isomorphism of Fréchet G-modules H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ M_dR^* ⊗_L π^* such that for every L-line ℒ ⊂ M_dR the preimage of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π^* in Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ is isomorphic to (Π_ℒ^an)^*, the resulting sequence 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → (Π_ℒ^an)^* → π^* → 0 being dual to Theorem 1.2's. Theorem 1.7 (= 9.9): Π(π, 0)^* carries a unique O(Ω)-module structure in which z acts as the operator ∂ with a^+ − 1 = u^+∂. Theorem 1.9: (O(Σ_n)^ρ)^{(p,0;0,1)=1} is isomorphic to the D(Γ)-module of µ ∈ H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗ V) with ∫_{1+p^nZ_p} µ ∈ H^1_e(G_{F_n}, V) for all n. Theorem 1.10: an infinitely primitivable function on Σ_n lies in O(Ω).

Add, as the de Rham layer that the étale layers build on: (1) V(π), M(π), M_dR(π), N_rig(π) and the parametrization V(π) ≅ Proj(M_dR(π)) with the identifications (5); (2) for non-trianguline V, Lemma 6.3 and Colmez's Proposition 6.4 (∂ = t^{-1}∇ bijective on N_rig(V)); (3) the local tools: Dospinescu's infinitesimal action (Theorem 7.3) and Colmez's Kirillov model (Definition 7.4, Proposition 7.6, the pairing {}_dif of Proposition 7.7, Colmez's duality formula Theorem 7.8, Proposition 7.9 and Theorem 7.11); (4) Π(π, 0): Proposition 8.2, Theorem 8.3, Proposition 8.4, Colmez's Theorem 8.5, the sheaf U ↦ tN_rig(π) ⊠ U, Theorem 8.6 and Definition 8.7, with Colmez's topological irreducibility of Π(π, 0) as a cited input; (5) the operator ∂ and the O(Ω)-module structure (Proposition 9.1, Theorem 9.4, Propositions 9.6, 9.10, Theorem 9.7, the operators T_f, Theorem 9.9, Proposition 9.16); (6) Φ: its existence (Theorem 5.1 = 8.8), surjectivity (Theorem 10.1, with the coadmissibility of O(Σ_n) over D(G)) and injectivity (Π(π, 2), Propositions 11.1–11.2, Theorem 11.3, Proposition 11.6, Theorem 11.7, Corollary 11.9, Proposition 11.10); (7) the corollaries: Remark 11.12 (weights 0, k + 1), Remark 11.13 (the conjecture as Breuil and Strauch formulated it, for the first cover, via Teitelbaum's model, Grosse-Klönne's Hyodo–Kato theory and Saito) and Proposition 12.2 (Hom_{D^b(D(G))}((Π(V)^an)^*, RΓ_dR(Σ_n)^ρ[1]) = D_dR(V) as filtered spaces). Record as expectations, not targets: Conjecture 12.4 (the boundary-function sheaf F_π on P^1(Q_p) is Colmez's U ↦ tN_rig(π) ⊠ U, and 0 → Π(π, 0)^* → tN_rig(π) ⊠ P^1 → Π(π, 2) → 0 is 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → F_π(P^1) → (Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ)^* → 0), the announced description of O(Σ_n)^ρ_∞ through B̃^+_rig (Remark 1.11), the Hyodo–Kato refinement of Remark 12.3, and the GL_2(F), GL_n(F) questions of Remark 1.3(b). Keep the hypotheses: π supercuspidal (essential, Remark 1.5; the trivial central character is not), Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1.

Import, never re-plan: PadicLocalLanglandsForGL2Qp R30.2–R30.5 (the Banach and locally analytic categories, the mod p correspondence, Colmez's D_rig(V) ⊠ P^1 with Theorem 7.1, the Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas description of locally algebraic vectors, Colmez–Dospinescu's universal completions, Π^univ); PadicHodgeTheory R06.2–R06.3 (Colmez–Fontaine, Fontaine's Weil–Deligne functor, Berger's N_rig, with the Fontaine–Berger descriptions routed to R06.3); PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.2, PG.4, PG.5 (D_rig, ψ, and Colmez's Iwasawa-cohomology statements routed to PG.5); the proposed ProetaleCohomologyOfPAdicCurvesAndTowers (the tower Σ_n, Stein and de Rham theory, Theorem 4.1, the uniformisation Theorem 5.7, Morita duality, Kohlhaase's bundles, Proposition 10.11); the proposed LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Frommer, Lemmas 5.9–5.10); CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31 (quaternionic local–global compatibility and Theorem 5.5); the proposed TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel (trianguline representations); GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3, R17.1, R17.3 (classical local Langlands, local and global Jacquet–Langlands). Prerequisites: Colmez's JEMS paper on change of weight [21], Colmez–Dospinescu [24], Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas [23], Dospinescu [28], [29]. Tests: Lemma 3.5's formulas on O(Ω); Theorem 9.7 for g = w (w∂w = ∂^{-1}); Theorem 1.4 for two distinct lines ℒ, ℒ′ recovering two non-isomorphic Π. Corrections the design must carry: Théorème 1.10 is false as printed and should conclude f ∈ H^0_dR(Σ_n)·O(Ω); its proof also needs Théorème 1.2 for nontrivial central character, which the paper only asserts (E9, E40). The uniqueness in Théorème 1.7 = 9.9 must be proved (E7). The proof of Théorème 5.1 must remove the unramified twist ξ by a global twist of finite order (E16). Proposition 7.7 b) holds with tN^+_dif,n, i.e. for k = 1, the only case used (E19). The proofs of Théorème 8.3 (injectivity of Res_{Z_p}), Proposition 8.4 a) (generation over the Robba ring of Γ), Théorème 9.7 (the right inverse) and Proposition 11.10 (the fixed radius) need the steps in E22, E24, E27 and E38. Coadmissibility is shown only for O(Σ_n)^ρ, not for all of O(Σ_n) (E30). Remarque 11.13 needs a third quaternionic form (E41).
routes.reason: The pending Part II owns the geometric realisation of the p-adic correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) in the Drinfeld tower, and its étale statement quotes this paper's theorem as an input; the de Rham realisation is the first layer of the same roadmap, not a new direction.

routes.title: Pro-étale cohomology of p-adic curves and of the Drinfeld tower
routes.brief: This route coalesces with ProetaleCohomologyOfPAdicCurvesAndTowers, proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B and extended by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-23; keep its id, title, area and brief. Dospinescu–Le Bras (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017)), §§3–5, 9.2 and 10, supply the analytic and de Rham geometry of the Drinfeld tower over Q_p that the roadmap's tower layer and its global method use. Add: (1) the tower Σ_n, the model over Q_p of p^ℤ\M̆_n with M̆_n = X^un[p^n] − X^un[ϖ_D^{2n−1}], its commuting G- and D^*-actions and Gal(Σ_n/Σ_0) = O_D^*/(1 + p^nO_D); (2) Stein spaces in any dimension: Fréchet(–Stein) structure, Kiehl's theorem, de Rham and compactly supported de Rham cohomology with Serre duality H^k_dR(X) ≅ H^{2d−k}_dR,c(X)^* (Grosse-Klönne, Chiarellotto), Proposition 3.1 and the G_i-stable Stein cover τ_n^{-1}(B_i); (3) the representation theory of functions on the tower: the twisted bundles O(k) with O(2) ⊗ det = Ω^1, Theorem 3.2 (O^{(k)}(Σ_n)^* is locally analytic) with Lemma 3.3, the formulas of Lemma 3.5, Proposition 3.6 and Remark 3.7 (H^1_dR,c of a smooth Stein curve with locally analytic action is smooth); (4) Theorem 4.1, dim Hom_G(π^*, H^1_dR(Σ_n)^ρ) = 2, by Čerednik–Drinfeld and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence with the degeneration of its ρ-part; (5) Theorem 5.7 with Lemma 5.8 (Hom_G(LA(X(K^p))^*, Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ) ≅ Ω^1(Sh_K)^ρ) and Remark 5.11 (the Hodge filtration); (6) Morita duality O(Ω)^* ≅ St^an and its transpose µ ↦ ∫ µ(x)/(z − x); (7) Kohlhaase's Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld bundles and Theorem 10.5, the projectivity of O(Σ_n) over O(Ω), Lemma 10.2 and Propositions 10.3, 10.8, 10.10 (O(Σ_n)^ρ is topologically irreducible as a G-equivariant O(Ω)-module with scalar endomorphisms); (8) Proposition 10.11: a continuous O(X)-linear map with dense image from a Fréchet O(X)-module to a finitely generated projective module over a Stein space X is surjective. Import Drinfeld's theorem and the Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformisation from HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.5, the Lubin–Tate tower from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a, the Schneider–Teitelbaum theory from the proposed LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, and the Steinberg representations from the proposed DrinfeldSymmetricSpacesAndSteinbergCohomology. Corrections the design must carry: the proof of Lemme 3.3 needs the open-mapping bound for multiplication by P′(f) (E12); the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence in the proof of Théorème 4.1 is for Γ_i/p^N Z, not Γ_i (E14); and the unramified twist dropped on p. 24 is treated in E16.
routes.reason: The pending roadmap already plans the tower M^ϖ_n, the analysis of Stein curves (Kiehl, Serre duality, Steinberg descriptions of O(Ω) and Ω^1(Ω)), the de Rham computations of the tower and the global method by p-adic uniformisation; the paper's §§3–5 and 10 are the same objects over Q_p.

routes.title: Locally analytic representations of p-adic reductive groups
routes.brief: This route coalesces with LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, proposed by PAPER-DING-25 and extended by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20; keep its id, title, area and brief. Dospinescu–Le Bras (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017)) uses the Schneider–Teitelbaum theory for GL_2(Q_p) and needs four statements that belong in this roadmap in their general form: (1) the distribution algebra D(H), Fréchet–Stein algebras and coadmissible modules, with Schneider–Teitelbaum's Lemma 3.6 (a finitely generated submodule of a coadmissible module is coadmissible), closed images and closedness of finitely generated ideals, and the density of locally analytic vectors in admissible Banach representations; (2) Frommer's description of D_h(G) as a finite free module over the closure U_h(𝔤) of U(𝔤) for uniform pro-p G, which the paper uses to show that a differentiable action with bounded derivatives on a Banach space is locally analytic (proof of Theorem 3.2); (3) Lemma 5.9: for a locally analytic representation W of compact type and λ ∈ W^*, w ↦ (g ↦ λ(g.w)) is continuous W → LA(G) (via Schneider–Teitelbaum, JAMS 2002, Prop. 3.2); (4) Lemma 5.10: in a locally convex space over a spherically complete field a sequence tends to 0 if and only if it tends weakly to 0. Import the underlying locally convex functional analysis rather than re-plan it. Correction the design must carry: in Frommer's description of D_h(G_i) (proof of Théorème 3.2) the constant is c_h = h − 1 + O(1), not c_h > p^{h−1}; the proof needs only p^{c_h} > C for h large (E11).
routes.reason: The pending roadmap plans the Schneider–Teitelbaum distribution algebra and coadmissible modules; the paper's uses of them are instances, and Frommer's theorem and Lemmas 5.9–5.10 are general facts of the same theory.

routes.title: The trianguline variety and its local model
routes.brief: This route coalesces with TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel, proposed by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 and extended by PAPER-DING-25 and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21; keep its id, title, area and brief. Dospinescu–Le Bras (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017)) needs only the two-dimensional base case over Q_p, from Colmez's 'Représentations triangulines de dimension 2' (Astérisque 319, 2008): the definition of a trianguline representation (D_rig(V) an extension of rank-one (φ, Γ)-modules after a finite extension of coefficients) and Colmez's lemme 3.2, that for an absolutely irreducible non-trianguline V the Frobenius φ has no eigenvector on D_rig(V). Plan it as the dimension-two case of the roadmap's trianguline (φ, Γ)-modules.
routes.reason: The pending roadmap plans trianguline (φ, Γ)-modules and triangulations; Colmez's two-dimensional definition and eigenvector criterion are its base case, which no layer of the atlas owns.

R31.1–R31.4 plan completed cohomology of modular and Shimura curves, its classical specialisations and Emerton's local–global compatibility (R31.4 names Emerton's unpublished manuscript). The paper writes out the same argument for the definite quaternion algebra B̄ split at p (the p-adic automorphic forms C^0(X) and Lemmas 4.4–4.7, the Hecke algebra and A, Theorem 5.4 with its appendix) and a globalisation of π (Theorem 5.5): the zero-dimensional case of those layers.

R06.3 plans the p-adic monodromy theorem and the bridge from de Rham representations to differential modules (RD.2 exports the analytic monodromy theorem to it). Berger's N_rig(V) and the Fontaine–Berger descriptions of D^+_dif, N^+_dif, N_rig and D_rig recalled in §6 are that bridge; the paper is a compact source for them.

PG.5 plans the ψ-complex and H^1_Iw ≅ D(T)^{ψ=1}. Colmez's D(Γ)-version over the Robba ring and his identification of (1 − φ)(tN_rig)^{ψ=1} with the Bloch–Kato-exponential subspace of H^1(G_{Q_p}, D(Γ) ⊗ V) are its analytic refinement.
RD.1 plans differential modules over the Robba ring; Kedlaya's duality between the cokernel and the kernel of ∂ is a statement of that layer.
R16.2 specialises local smooth representation theory to GL_2, including the explicit supercuspidal descriptions; Henniart's unicity of types for GL_2 is a statement of that layer.

review.reason: Both passages checked on the page images. Φ : Π(π, 0)^* → O(Σ_n)^ρ is O(Ω)-linear, so twisting by det g·(a − c∂)^{-2} gives a map into O(2)(Σ_n)^ρ ⊗ det = Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ. sourceIssues.locator: §5.1, proof of Lemme 5.6, p. 27 (arXiv v2); p. 351 (Annals)
sourceIssues.printed: Soit χ un caractère de Hecke χ de F tel que η̄_p = ω_2^{r+1}, χ_∞(z) = z^{−1} et χ_ℓ choisi de sorte que l'induite automorphe locale (pour le groupe GL_2) Ind_{F_ℓ}^{Q_ℓ} χ_ℓ soit supercuspidale.
sourceIssues.correction: Soit χ un caractère de Hecke de F et η : G_F → Q̄_p^* le caractère galoisien p-adique associé à χ par la théorie du corps de classes, tels que (η|_{G_{F_p}})‾ = ω_2^{r+1} à twist non ramifié près (F_p = Q_{p²}, p inerte), χ_∞(z) = z^{-1} … Then r̄_p = Ind_{Q_{p²}}^{Q_p}(η|_{G_{F_p}})‾. Here η is taken in the normalization matching the paper's r; if r is normalized as the dual, replace η by η^{-1}. Stated on the automorphic side, the condition would be χ̄_p|_{O_{F_p}^*} = ω_2^{r+1} times the reduction of τ, not χ̄_p = ω_2^{r+1}.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed as a misprint: η is defined nowhere in the proof, and χ is the only character in the construction. The recorded correction ('χ̄_p = ω_2^{r+1}, a condition on the reduction of χ's component at p') needs refining. Taken literally as a condition on the automorphic local component χ_p on O_{F_p}^*, it gives the wrong result, because the infinity type χ_∞(z) = z^{-1} contributes to the Galois character on inertia. For u ∈ O_{F_p}^*, η(Art(u)) = χ_p(u)·u^{±1} (via the embedding F_p → Q̄_p), so η̄|_{I_p} = χ̄_p·ω_2^{±1} (or ω_2^{±p}, depending on the embedding). Imposing χ̄_p = ω_2^{r+1} would then make r̄_p induced from ω_2^{r+1±1} or ω_2^{r+1±p}, which is not an unramified twist of Ind ω_2^{r+1}. So the condition must be on the Galois character, which is presumably what 'η' denotes. The doubled 'χ ... χ' in the same sentence is a further trivial slip. In the authors' defence, the intended meaning is clear from the preceding sentence, which prescribes r̄_p.

review.reason: Revised on re-reading; independent check: Checked on the p. 27 image at 400 dpi. The text reads 'Soit χ un caractère de Hecke χ de F tel que \overline{η_p} = ω_2^{r+1}, χ_∞(z) = z^{-1} et χ_ℓ choisi …'. The η on p. 27 is the only η in the whole text layer, so η is never defined. The doubled 'χ … χ' is also on the page. The revision is right, and the ledger correction ('χ̄_p = ω_2^{r+1}, a condition on the reduction of χ's component at p') is wrong or meaningless if χ_p is read as the automorphic local component. (i) χ_p takes non-integral values on F_p^*. Since χ is trivial on F^* and χ_∞(p) = p^{-1}, we get χ_p(p) = p·(root of unity), which has valuation 1, so 'χ̄_p' is not defined on F_p^*. (ii) On O_{F_p}^* it is defined, but it differs from the Galois character on inertia. The p-adic avatar is ψ(x) = χ_fin(x)·τ(x_p)^{-1}, where τ: F_p = Q_{p²} → Q̄_p comes from the fixed embeddings. It is trivial on F^* because χ_fin(α) = α. For u ∈ O_{F_p}^* this gives ψ(u) = χ_p(u)·τ(u)^{-1}, so ψ̄|_{I} = χ̄_p·ω_2^{ε} with ε ∈ {±1, ±p}, depending on the embedding and the sign convention for Art. Imposing χ̄_p = ω_2^{r+1} would give r̄_p|_I = ω_2^{a} ⊕ ω_2^{pa} with a = r+1+ε. This is an unramified twist of Ind ω_2^{r+1} only if a ≡ r+1 or p(r+1) mod p²−1. Reducing mod p−1 forces p−1 | 1, which is impossible for odd p. (For p = 2 some conventions coincide by accident.) So the condition must be on the reduction of the Galois character attached to χ, restricted to G_{Q_{p²}}. Presumably that is what η denotes, and it makes r̄_p = Ind_{Q_{p²}}^{Q_p}(η|_{G_{F_p}})‾ the induced representation the preceding sentence asks for. The intended meaning is recoverable from that sentence, so this is a misprint that affects nothing.

review.reason: I checked the quotations on the images of pp. 9 and 48; the proof is on p. 51. Théorème 1.7 and Théorème 9.9 both assert that the structure is unique. The proof ('Le théorème 9.9 se déduit maintenant facilement…', p. 51) sets f·l := T_f(l) and checks only (fg)·l = f·(g·l). Uniqueness is never addressed. With the literal statement, which has no continuity condition, it is not a formality. The structure is forced on L[z] and on the units 1/(z − x), x ∈ Q_p, which must act as (∂ − x)^{-1}. But a ring homomorphism O(Ω) → End_L(Π(π, 0)^*) is not determined by a dense subalgebra. With continuity of f ↦ f·l, which the constructed structure has (Proposition 9.15 b)), uniqueness follows at once from the density of S (p. 50). Without continuity it is still true, a posteriori, as the first reading says; I re-derived it. For a ∈ Ω(L′), write f − f(a) = (z − a)h in O(Ω)_{L′}. Two structures then differ on f by (∂ − a) times their difference on h. Iterating, the difference lands in ∩_k(∂ − a)^k Π(π, 0)^*_{L′}. By Théorème 1.2 and Proposition 9.16 (whose proof gives Φ∘∂ = z·Φ), this is ∩_k(z − a)^k O(Σ_n)^ρ_{L′}. That intersection is 0: Σ_n → Ω is étale, and each connected component of Σ_{n,L′} maps onto the connected Ω_{L′}, so it contains a point over a, where z − a is a local parameter; the identity principle then applies. This argument uses only the existence part, so it is not circular. Uniqueness is not used later: Proposition 9.16 and §§10–11 use the constructed structure and its continuity. Kind: gap is right. Reach: 'nothing' understates it. The uniqueness claim of a numbered theorem, stated twice, has no proof at all. But the paper's own results fill it in a few lines (or the statement can add continuity), so the reach is the proof of Théorème 9.9, not the stated result. The same place also has: Checked on pp. 48, 51 and 9. Théorème 9.9 (« une unique structure de O(Ω)-module … compatible avec sa structure de L-espace vectoriel ») and Théorème 1.7 (« qui étend sa structure de L-espace vectoriel ») both claim uniqueness with no topological condition. The proof (p. 51) constructs f·l = T_f(l) and says that « le seul point qu'il nous reste à vérifier » is (fg)·l = f·(g·l). Uniqueness is never argued. As printed it is not immediate. Another structure ·' must agree with T on R = L[z, (z − x)^{-1} : x ∈ Q_p], because z − x is a unit of O(Ω) and ∂ − x is invertible. For f ∈ O(Ω) and any nonzero P ∈ L[z], interpolation on the finite subscheme V(P) ∩ Ω gives f = r + P·h with r ∈ L[z] and h ∈ O(Ω). So T_f − (f·') has image in ∩_P P(∂)Π(π,0)*. Nothing available in §9 shows that this intersection is 0; the paper itself says (p. 9) that the O(Ω)-module structure of Π(π,0)* is known only as a corollary of the final result. The clause is nevertheless true. (i) For a module structure with f ↦ f·l continuous, uniqueness follows in one line: 1/(z − x) must act as (∂ − x)^{-1}, so f acts as T_f on S, and S is dense (p. 50). (ii) For the algebraic statement, Φ is injective (§11) and O(Ω)-linear for T (Prop. 9.16), so it sends ∩_P P(∂)Π(π,0)* into ∩_P P·O(Σ_n)^ρ = 0. Nothing later uses uniqueness: Prop. 9.16, §10 and §11 use only the constructed T_f and Prop. 9.15. So the gap does not spread, but it sits in the uniqueness clause of Théorème 9.9 = 1.7 itself, which the paper states and never proves. Unlike E27, the algebraic clause cannot be closed from what §9 has available. 'Gap; affects a stated result' is right.

sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample from the paper's own description. By p. 3, Σ_0 is two copies of Ω, with O_D^* acting trivially and ϖ_D exchanging them. By footnote 16, O(Ω) ≅ O(Σ_0)^{D^*} sits in O(Σ_0) ⊂ O(Σ_n) diagonally. Let e ∈ O(Σ_0) be 1 on one copy and −1 on the other. (Over Q_p, where the copies are exchanged by Frobenius, take instead e = α ∈ Q_{p²} with σ(α) = −α.) Since de = 0 and z ∈ O(Ω) (∞ ∉ Ω), e = (d/dz)^k(e·z^k/k!) for every k, so e is infinitely primitivable on Σ_0 and, by pullback, on every Σ_n. But ϖ_D·e = −e, so e ∉ O(Ω). More generally, e_χ·z^m is a counterexample for every nontrivial character χ∘Nrd occurring in H^0_dR(Σ_n); D^* acts on the geometric components through Nrd ([79], [37]). The failing step is the appeal to Théorème 1.2, which needs π_i supercuspidal, that is, dim ρ_i > 1. Footnote 11 itself uses dim ρ > 1 to get H^0_dR(Σ_n)^ρ = 0. For a nontrivial one-dimensional ρ_i, JL^{-1}(ρ_i) is a twist of the Steinberg representation, and O(Σ_n)^{ρ_i} = e_χ·O(Ω) contains e_χ·L[z], all of which are infinitely primitivable. The argument does prove the corrected statement for the ρ_i of dimension > 1, subject to the next entry. Defence: if 'f ∈ O(Ω)' is read loosely as 'on each geometric component, f comes from a function on Ω', the statement is true. But the proof explicitly identifies O(Ω) with the trivial isotypic part ('ρ_i soit triviale, i.e. que f ∈ O(Ω)'), so the printed statement is false as written. Théorème 1.10 is a stand-alone corollary and nothing else in the paper depends on it.

review.reason: I checked the quotations on the images of pp. 11 and 66. I also checked the conventions on pp. 3, 4, 9 (footnote 16), 13 (§2 (5)–(6)), 14–15 (§3.1) and 23. (1) Σ_0. On p. 3, Σ_0 is 'deux copies de Ω, avec action triviale de O_D^*, l'élément ϖ_D permutant les deux copies'. By §3.1 the Weil descent datum is the canonical one composed with the shift by 1, so over Q_p, Σ_0 ≅ Ω ⊗_{Q_p} Q_{p²}. O(X) means L ⊗_{Q_p} H^0(X, O_X) (§2 (6)). (2) O(Ω) inside O(Σ_n). Footnote 16 says 'O(Ω) ≃ O(Σ_0)^{D^*} (… plongement diagonal …)'. The proof on p. 66 ends 'ρ_i soit triviale, i.e. que f ∈ O(Ω)'. So O(Ω) is the D^*-invariant part, which is the trivial isotypic part for σ^ρ = Hom_{D^*}(ρ, σ) (p. 4). D^* acts on Σ_n through the finite group D^*/p^Z(1 + p^nO_D), so the decomposition f = Σ v_i ⊗ f_i is legitimate. (3) 'Infinitement primitivable' (p. 11) means f ∈ Im((d/dz)^k) for every k, where d/dz comes from Ω^1(Σ_n) = O(Σ_n)dz. No condition excludes locally constant functions. Counterexample: H^0_dR(Σ_0) = L ⊗ Q_{p²} has L-dimension 2, while its intersection with O(Ω) is H^0_dR(Ω) = L, because Ω is geometrically connected. Take e = α ∈ Q_{p²} with σ(α) = −α; if Q_{p²} ⊂ L, e is ±α on the two copies. ϖ_D acts on O(Σ_0) = O(Ω) ⊗ Q_{p²} O(Ω)-linearly (footnote 16) and nontrivially (it swaps the geometric components), so it acts by σ on the second factor. Hence ϖ_D·e = −e, and e ∉ O(Ω). Since de = 0 and z ∈ O(Ω) (∞ ∈ P^1(Q_p) is not in Ω), e = (d/dz)^k(e z^k/k!) for every k. The same holds after pullback to every Σ_n, and for e·z^m. So Théorème 1.10 is false for every n. The character involved is χ∘Nrd with χ unramified and χ(p) = −1 (Nrd ϖ_D = −p). It has trivial central character (χ(x²) = 1), so no convention on central characters excludes it. The failing step is 'puisque ρ_i est non triviale, on peut appliquer le théorème 1.2' on p. 66. Théorème 1.2 needs π supercuspidal, i.e. dim ρ > 1. A nontrivial one-dimensional ρ = χ∘Nrd corresponds to a twist of the Steinberg representation. The paper itself uses dim ρ > 1 to get H^0_dR(Σ_n)^ρ = 0 (footnote 11), notes that D^* acts on the geometric components through Nrd (p. 23), and says that the Steinberg case has H^0_dR ≠ 0 (Remarque 1.5). Defence: the statement is true if 'f ∈ O(Ω)' is read as 'on each geometric component, f is the pullback of a function on Ω'. But footnote 16 and the last line of the proof fix the stricter meaning. So this is an error, not a misprint. Théorème 1.10 is not used elsewhere: it is cited only on pp. 10, 64 (Remarque 11.11) and 66. The reach is this stated result. The same place also has: Confirmed on the images: p. 11 has 'Soit f ∈ O(Σ_n) une fonction infiniment primitivable sur Σ_n. Alors f ∈ O(Ω)'. The proof on p. 66 applies Théorème 1.2 to every nontrivial ρ_i ('puisque ρ_i est non triviale, on peut appliquer le théorème 1.2') and concludes 'ρ_i soit triviale, i.e. que f ∈ O(Ω)'. Théorème 1.2 needs π_i = JL(ρ_i) supercuspidal, that is dim ρ_i > 1. For a nontrivial character ρ = χ∘Nrd, JL(ρ) is a twist of the Steinberg representation, and footnote 11 (p. 6) itself says that H^0_dR(Σ_n)^ρ = 0 uses dim ρ > 1. Here is my own counterexample from the paper's definitions. By p. 3, Σ_0 is two copies of Ω, with O_D^* acting trivially and ϖ_D exchanging the copies. By footnote 16 (p. 9), O(Ω) ≅ O(Σ_0)^{D^*} sits diagonally in O(Σ_0) ⊂ O(Σ_n), and u^+ = −d/dz on O(Σ_n) (p. 19). Let f = (1, −1) on Σ_0, pulled back to Σ_n. Since ∞ ∉ Ω, z ∈ O(Ω), and f = (d/dz)^k(z^k/k!, −z^k/k!) for every k. So f is infinitely primitivable, but ϖ_D f = −f, so f ∉ O(Ω). This f lies in the isotypic part of the sign character of D^*/p^Z O_D^*, which is trivial on p since v(Nrd p) = 2. The counterexample does not depend on how the copies are defined over Q_p: if they are exchanged by Frobenius, take the constant α ∈ Q_{p²} with σ(α) = −α instead. More generally, every locally constant function on Σ_n is infinitely primitivable. The argument does prove that the components along ρ_i with dim ρ_i > 1 vanish. That holds subject to Théorème 1.2 for supercuspidal π_i with nontrivial central character, which the paper only asserts (Remarque 1.3(a)); that is a separate issue. So the corrected statement is the one proposed. Théorème 1.10 is a stand-alone corollary, and nothing else depends on it.

Its image is a finite submodule, hence closed (BGR 3.7.2), so by the open mapping theorem ‖P′(f)y‖ ≥ c‖y‖. Since Q_n → P′(f), for n large ‖Q_n y‖ ≥ (c/2)‖y‖. Hence x_n is bounded, P′(f)x_n = Q_nx_n − (Q_n − P′(f))x_n → −∂_𝔛(P)(f), and ‖x_n − x_m‖ ≤ c^{−1}‖P′(f)(x_n − x_m)‖ → 0, so lim x_n exists.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed on the images (pp. 17–18). The proof puts x_n = (f_n − f)/p^n and gets Q_n x_n → −∂_𝔛(P)(f), where Q_n = (P(f_n) − P(f))/(f_n − f), read as the polynomial difference quotient, since f_n − f need not be invertible. It then concludes from 'lim Q_n = P′(f) ≠ 0' that lim x_n exists. That inference holds only if multiplication by P′(f) is bounded below on O(U_i), for instance if P′(f) is a unit, and P′(f) is in general not a unit. If P_f has degree d ≥ 2 and t ∈ O(U_{0,i}) is a nonzero non-unit, then tf has minimal polynomial t^d P_f(X/t) and P′_{tf}(tf) = t^{d−1}P′_f(f), which is not a unit. Degree ≥ 2 does occur, since Σ_n → Σ_0 has degree > 1. Also, P′(f) ≠ 0 is automatic in characteristic 0, so 'puisque le revêtement est étale' does not supply what the argument needs. The final comparison P′(f)(lim x_n − ∂_𝔛 f) = 0 only needs P′(f) to be a non-zero-divisor, which is true when P is taken componentwise over the normal domains making up O(U_{0,i}). The lemma is true: the missing step is supplied by the standard affinoid argument in the correction. So this is a gap in the proof, not a false statement.

sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed on the image (p. 23). N is chosen with p^N ∈ Γ_i, and M̆_{n,N} = p^{NZ}\M̆_n. So p^N ∈ Γ_i acts trivially on M̆_{n,N}, and the Galois group of M̆_{n,N} → Γ_i\M̆_{n,N} is Γ̄_i = Γ_i/p^{NZ}, not Γ_i. With Γ_i, the Hochschild–Serre sequence computes Γ_i-equivariant cohomology, not H_dR(Sh_K). The difference is real. It is an error rather than a misprint because the displayed spectral sequence is false and the fix changes the group in three displays. The intended object, Hochschild–Serre for the Galois cover named in the text, is still clear. Defence: the proof uses only the ρ-part, where only q = 1 survives, and only E_2^{0,1}. There H^0(Γ_i, ·) = H^0(Γ̄_i, ·) and Hom_G = Hom_{G/p^{NZ}} on representations where p^N acts trivially; p^N does act trivially on X(K^p), since p^N ∈ Γ_i means p^N ∈ K^p. So (2), (3) and Théorème 4.1 are unaffected.

Choose a Dirichlet character ψ of modulus prime to p with ψ(p) = ξ(p)^{-1}; for instance take modulus p^m − 1, m = ord ξ(p), and extend p ↦ ξ(p)^{-1} from ⟨p⟩ ≅ Z/m. Replace f by f ⊗ (χ_ψ∘Nrd), shrinking K^p and enlarging Σ. The new form has weight 2, r̄ = r̄_f ⊗ ψ̄ is still absolutely irreducible on G_{Q_p}, and π(f)_p = π. Then Ω^1(Sh_K)^ρ[𝔭] ≠ 0 (global Jacquet–Langlands, JL(π) = ρ), and Π(𝔭) ∈ V(π) (Π(𝔭)^lisse ≅ π(f)_p by Théorème 5.4 and Lemme 4.7). Make the same replacement on p. 24.

This fails whenever ξ(p)² ≠ 1, because the central characters are ξ² and 1. It fails in general for the unramified quadratic ξ as well. Likewise Π(𝔭)^lisse ≅ π(f)_p (Théorème 5.4 with Lemme 4.7) puts Π(𝔭) in V(π ⊗ ξ∘det) = V(π) ⊗ ξ∘det. It is repaired by a global twist. ξ has finite order: π(f)_∞ is trivial (weight 2, definite B̄), so the central character of π(f) is a character of the profinite group A^*/Q^*R^*, hence of finite order, and its p-component is ξ²·ω_π = ξ². A character of the subgroup ⟨p⟩ with p ↦ ξ(p)^{-1} extends to a Dirichlet character ψ of modulus p^m−1, which is prime to p, so the idelic χ satisfies χ_p = ξ^{-1}∘(unramified). It is repaired by a global twist. ξ has finite order: π(f)_∞ is trivial (weight 2, definite B̄), so the central character of π(f) is a character of the profinite group A^*/Q^*R^*, hence of finite order, and its p-component is ξ²·ω_π = ξ². Let m be the order of ξ(p). The class of p has order exactly m in (Z/(p^m−1))^*. A character of the subgroup ⟨p⟩ with p ↦ ξ(p)^{-1} extends to a Dirichlet character ψ of modulus p^m−1, which is prime to p, so the idelic χ satisfies χ_p = ξ^{-1}∘(unramified). Replace f by f ⊗ (χ∘Nrd), shrinking K^p and enlarging Σ. This preserves weight 2 (Nrd > 0 on B̄^*(R)), and r̄ becomes r̄_f ⊗ ψ̄, whose restriction to G_{Q_p} is still absolutely irreducible. Now π(f)_p = π, so every step of §5.3 holds as written. The same unexplained removal of ξ occurs on p. 24 ('Du théorème 5.5, on déduit … π(f)_p = π', in the proof of Théorème 4.1). In the authors' defence, they flag the twist explicitly, and the repair is standard. Théorème 5.1 itself is unaffected.

review.reason: Checked on the p. 29 image: 'Puisque D(G) et W sont tous deux des espaces de Fréchet, on peut tester la continuité de F^* avec des suites.' In Lemme 5.9, W is a space of compact type. An infinite-dimensional space of compact type is never metrizable: a Fréchet space whose strong dual is also Fréchet is normable, and a normable Montel space is finite-dimensional. In the application W = ((Ω^1(Σ_n))^ρ)^* is infinite-dimensional. Ω^1(Σ_n)^ρ is nonzero (pp. 29–30), and u^+ acts injectively on it (p. 30, Lemme 3.5). On a nonzero finite-dimensional locally analytic G-representation, u^+ would act nilpotently, which is impossible here. Checking continuity on sequences needs only the source D(G) to be metrizable. sourceIssues.reason: Checked on p. 56. The literal defect is real. In the case used (X = Ω, a curve), every irreducible component of V(f_1) ∩ U_j is a point. A 0-dimensional component {z} of V(f_1, …, f_{i−1}) ∩ U_j stays a component of V(f_1, …, f_{i−1}) ∩ U_{j'} for every j' ≥ j: the cover is increasing, and U_j is an admissible open, so a positive-dimensional component through z would meet U_j in positive dimension. The recipe « pour chaque composante un point … Répétant cette opération pour chaque j » therefore picks the same z for every j' ≥ j. For such a repeated point, no ξ_k can vanish at the earlier copy and not at z_k. But nothing is missing mathematically: the z_n are clearly meant to enumerate the countable set of chosen points without repetition. The only property used afterwards, that each component of each V(f_1, …, f_{i−1}) ∩ U_j contains some z_n, survives removing duplicates. For pairwise distinct points, ξ_k exists by the paper's own hint (or by Theorem B), and if the set is finite the sum defining f_i is finite. The wording omits the distinctness of the z_n; the meaning is clear and the mathematics is right as intended, so this is a misprint that affects nothing, not a gap in the proof.

sourceIssues.printed: Comme v′ ∈ Im(u^+)^j pour tout j > 0, z_1 est infiniment divisible par t. On voit immédiatement que cela force z_1 = 0 en prenant une base de N_rig(π) sur R.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the fixed radius: Π(π,0)^* ⊂ tN^{]0,r_n]} ⊠ P^1 for one n (p. 59; [24, cor. VI.13]). If v′ = (u^+)^j y_j with y_j ∈ Π(π,0)^*, then z_1 = t^j Res_{Z_p}(y_j) with Res_{Z_p}(y_j) ∈ tN^{]0,r_n]} for all j. So each coordinate of z_1 (in a basis of N^{]0,r_n]}) vanishes to infinite order at the zeros ζ_{p^m} − 1 of t lying in that annulus, hence z_1 = 0. The same applies to z_2 via w, and in Remarque 12.1.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed on the image (p. 64). As v′ = (u^+)^j y_j with y_j ∈ Π(π,0)^*, and u^+ multiplies the Res_{Z_p}-component by t (proof of Proposition 9.1: u^+(x, y) = (tx, −t∂²y)), z_1 = t^j Res_{Z_p}(y_j) for every j. The paper concludes z_1 = 0 'en prenant une base de N_rig(π) sur R'. That reduces the claim to ∩_j t^j R = 0 in the Robba ring, which is false. For the counterexample, let f = ∏_{m≥1}(Φ_{p^m}(1+T)/p)^m. Write (1+T)^{p^{m−1}} = 1 + u_m, with |u_m|_ρ → 0 on |T| ≤ ρ < 1. Then |Φ_p(1+u_m)/p − 1|_ρ ≤ max(|u_m|_ρ, p|u_m|_ρ^{p−1}) → 0, and |g^m − 1|_ρ ≤ |g − 1|_ρ when |g − 1|_ρ < 1. So the product converges on the open unit disc, and f(0) = 1, so f ≠ 0. It vanishes to order m at each ζ_{p^m} − 1, and t = T∏_m Φ_{p^m}(1+T)/p has simple zeros there. Hence f/t^j is analytic on the annulus beyond the zeros of level < j, that is f ∈ t^j R for every j. The step is still true, by a fact the paper records on p. 59 but does not invoke: Π(π,0)^* ⊂ tN^{]0,r_n]} ⊠ P^1 for one fixed n ([24, cor. VI.13], p. 38). Then every coordinate of z_1 is a function on a fixed annulus. It is divisible by t^j there for all j, so it vanishes to infinite order at a zero ζ_{p^m} − 1 of t in that annulus, and hence it is 0. Remarque 12.1 ('satisfait trivialement Res_{Z_p}(z) = 0', p. 67) rests on the same point, via the fixed radius r_{m(V)} for (Π^an)^*. Reclassification: the gap is real, but the justification the paper gives is not just terse, it is invalid as written. So the proof of Proposition 11.10 is affected until the fixed-radius argument is supplied, even though Proposition 11.10 itself is true. The same fact also follows from [31] (Remarque 11.11). This matches how the other invalid-inference gaps with short repairs were classed (E12, E27).

sourceIssues.correction: The step needs Théorème 1.2 for supercuspidal π_i with nontrivial central character. The paper only asserts this, in Remarque 1.3(a). Either prove that case, or restrict Théorème 1.10 (as corrected in E9) to the components along ρ_i whose central character is the square of a character of Q_p^* trivial on p² (for p odd: ω(−1) = 1). Those components reduce to trivial central character by multiplying by a locally constant unit e_χ at a deeper level.
sourceIssues.reason: Σ_n → Σ_0 is Galois with group O_D^*/(1 + p^nO_D), so every irreducible representation of that finite group occurs in O(Σ_n). For p odd and n = 1 this group is F_{p²}^* ⋉ F_{p²}. Among its representations are the (p + 1)-dimensional ones Ind(η ⊗ ψ), with ψ a nontrivial additive character and η an arbitrary character of F_p^* = Z_p^*/(1 + pZ_p). So constituents ρ_i of dimension > 1 on which the centre Z_p^* acts by any character η occur. Théorème 1.2 is proved only for trivial central character (§2 (5)); its proof relies on det V = χ_cyc, the globalisation of §5 and Colmez's results in that setting. Defence: if the central character is a square χ², multiplying by the locally constant unit e_χ on a deeper level reduces the claim to trivial central character. But η need not be a square: take η a generator of the character group of F_p^*, which has even order p − 1. The authors state that the extension holds, and it is plausible, so this is a gap rather than an error.

review.reason: I checked the quotations on the images of pp. 4 and 66. The gap is real. Théorème 1.2 assumes π supercuspidal with trivial central character, and §2 (5) (p. 13) fixes such a π. Its proof uses this repeatedly: det V(Π) = χ_cyc 'car le caractère central de π est trivial' (p. 5); 'H^k_dR,c(Σ_n, N)^{ρ∨} = H^k_dR,c(Σ_n)^{ρ∨} puisque le caractère central de ρ est trivial' (p. 23); δ_V = 1 (p. 35); π is projective among the smooth representations with trivial central character (p. 64). Remarque 1.3(a) only asserts that this hypothesis 'n'est pas essentielle'. The proof of 1.10 applies Théorème 1.2 to every ρ_i occurring in O(Σ_n), and ρ_i with dim > 1 and nontrivial central character do occur. p acts trivially on Σ_n, but Z_p^* ⊂ Z(D^*) need not. I re-derived the first reading's example (p odd, n = 1). O_D^*/(1 + pO_D) ≅ F_{p²}^* ⋉ F_{p²}, and x acts by y ↦ x^{p−1}y (from ϖ_D x = σ(x)ϖ_D). The stabiliser of a nontrivial additive character ψ is F_p^*. So the irreducible representations Ind(η ⊗ ψ) have dimension p + 1, for every character η of F_p^*, and the central F_p^* (the image of Z_p^*) acts by η. The sum of the squares of the dimensions checks: (p² − 1) + (p − 1)²(p + 1)² = p²(p² − 1). Σ_1 → Σ_0 is Galois with this group (p. 3), and Σ_0 is Stein. So every irreducible representation of the group occurs in O(Σ_1): each isotypic part becomes nonzero after the faithfully flat base change to O(Σ_1). The first reading's reduction also checks. Multiplying by a locally constant unit e_χ at a deeper level commutes with d/dz and changes the central character by χ². So a square central character ω reduces to the trivial case. For p odd, ω is a square if and only if ω(−1) = 1: the character group of μ_{p−1} is cyclic of even order, and (1 + pZ_p)/(1 + p^nZ_p) has odd order. When η(−1) = −1, as for a generator η, nothing in the paper covers the component. It is not an error: the extension is asserted by the authors and plausible. Reach: I would change 'the proof' to 'a stated result'. Filling the gap is not a routine step. It needs Théorème 1.2 for supercuspidal π with nontrivial central character, which means redoing the main theorem without det V = χ_cyc. So Théorème 1.10 (even as corrected in E9) is not established by the paper for these components. This matches the treatment of the parallel gap for the coadmissibility of all of O(Σ_n) (§10, p.

Alors on a [BS(ℒ″)] = a[BS(ℒ)] + b[BS(ℒ′)] et [Π^an_{ℒ″}] = a[Π^an_ℒ] + b[Π^an_{ℒ′}] dans le groupe Ext^1_G((O(Σ_n)^ρ)^*, π). Donc BS(ℒ″) = Π^an_{ℒ″}.

sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed on the images (pp. 65–66). Let E be the extension 0 → π ⊗ M_dR → (Ω^1(Σ)^ρ)^* → (O(Σ)^ρ)^* → 0, the dual of 0 → O^ρ → Ω^{1,ρ} → H^1_dR,ρ → 0 after an identification H^1_dR(Σ)^ρ ≅ π^* ⊗ M_dR(π)^*. The class of the dual of the preimage of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π^* is then Ψ(λ) := (id ⊗ λ)_*E, for a generator λ of ℒ^⊥ ⊂ M_dR^*. So BS(ℒ) and Π^an_ℒ (Théorème 1.4, Corollaire 11.9) come from two linear maps Ψ_BS and Ψ_DLB : M_dR^* → Ext^1_G((O(Σ)^ρ)^*, π). These are built from the Hyodo–Kato/Saito identification and from the identification of Théorème 1.4. They differ by some γ ∈ GL(M_dR^*): Aut_G(π^* ⊗ M_dR^*) = GL(M_dR^*) by Schur, and no compatibility between the two identifications is known a priori, which is exactly the content of the conjecture. For an extension of Π(π,0) by π, 'BS(ℒ) ≅ Π^an_ℒ' means only that the classes are proportional, since End(π) = End(Π(π,0)) = L. The two global forms therefore give Ψ_BS(e) = λΨ_DLB(e) and Ψ_BS(e′) = μΨ_DLB(e′), with e ∈ ℒ^⊥, e′ ∈ ℒ′^⊥ and unknown λ, μ ∈ L^*. The two displays write [BS(ℒ″)] = a[BS(ℒ)] + b[BS(ℒ′)] and [Π^an_{ℒ″}] = a[Π^an_ℒ] + b[Π^an_{ℒ′}] with the same (a, b), and then conclude that the two classes agree. That needs λ = μ. Otherwise, for ab ≠ 0, aλΨ_DLB(e) + bμΨ_DLB(e′) is not proportional to aΨ_DLB(e) + bΨ_DLB(e′), because Ψ_DLB(e) and Ψ_DLB(e′) are independent, distinct lines giving non-isomorphic Π^an. A 'base (ℒ, ℒ′)' fixes two points of P^1, and two points do not determine a projective linear map. Defence: the conclusion is true once a third global form with a third line is used. The text already asserts that forms with different filtrations exist by varying the residual representation, and the same input gives a third. So this is a gap in the argument of the remark, not a false claim. Also, P(M_dR) is P^1(L), not P^1(Q_p).

review.reason: Confirmed on the 300 dpi crop (p. 66): 'On a donc un autre ℒ′ pour lequel on sait que Π^an_{ℒ′} = BS(ℒ).' The global argument, rerun for the second quaternionic form, gives BS(ℒ′) = Π^an_{ℒ′}. The next displays use [BS(ℒ′)] and [Π^an_{ℒ′}] as the second basis vectors. As printed, the claim would contradict the first case: BS(ℒ) = Π^an_ℒ ≇ Π^an_{ℒ′} for ℒ′ ≠ ℒ, since Π^an determines V ([24]).
